sections.subtitle: Puč ili vladavina prava: Poljska u središtu političke oluje
sections.screenshot_description: Voditeljica uvodi temu sukoba predsjednika Nawrockog i premijera Tuska
sections.content:
Podcast **„Mrežnica“** Radija Mrežnica ovaj put se bavi Poljskom, zemljom koju voditeljica naziva jednom od velikih europskih sila. Gost emisije je poljsko-hrvatski novinar **Goran Andrijanić**, koji se razgovoru priključuje iz Varšave. Na početku razgovora gost publiku pozdravlja na poljskom, s „Dzień dobry“, a voditeljica pozdrav ponavlja i provjerava je li ga dobro izgovorila.

Voditeljica odmah otvara središnju dilemu ovih dana. Prema njezinim riječima, Poljska je u glavnim medijima, ne samo hrvatskim, pomalo stavljena po strani, iako se ondje događaju iznimno zanimljive stvari. Tabor predsjednika **Nawrockog** govori o pokušaju puča. Tabor premijera **Tuska** tvrdi da je riječ samo o vraćanju onoga što bi po zakonu trebalo biti.

Kako bi naglasila važnost teme, voditeljica nabraja što Poljsku čini posebnom:
- jedna je od najjačih, a gospodarski gotovo i najjača zemlja Europske unije,
- treća je po snazi u NATO savezu,
- i dalje ima vlastitu valutu, zlot,
- njezina središnja banka gomila zlato,
- čini se da nema problema s ilegalnim migracijama kakve muče ostatak zapadne Europe.
sections.subtitle_en: Coup or Rule of Law: Poland at the Center of a Political Storm
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host introduces the topic of the conflict between President Nawrocki and Prime Minister Tusk
sections.content_en:
The podcast **“Mrežnica”** of Radio Mrežnica this time deals with Poland, a country the host calls one of the great European powers. The guest of the show is the Polish-Croatian journalist **Goran Andrijanić**, who joins the conversation from Warsaw. At the beginning of the conversation, the guest greets the audience in Polish with “Dzień dobry”, and the host repeats the greeting and checks whether she pronounced it correctly.

The host immediately opens the central dilemma of these days. According to her words, Poland has been somewhat sidelined in the mainstream media, not only Croatian, even though extremely interesting things are happening there. The camp of President **Nawrocki** speaks of an attempted coup. The camp of Prime Minister **Tusk** claims that it is merely about restoring what should be according to the law.

In order to emphasize the importance of the topic, the host lists what makes Poland special:
- it is one of the strongest, and economically almost the strongest country in the European Union,
- it is the third strongest in the NATO alliance,
- it still has its own currency, the zloty,
- its central bank is hoarding gold,
- it seems to have no problems with illegal migration such as those troubling the rest of Western Europe.

sections.subtitle: Dvadeset godina rata dvaju tabora: od 2005. do danas
sections.screenshot_description: Goran Andrijanić objašnjava početak sukoba 2005. godine
sections.content:
Andrijanić objašnjava da aktualna kriza nije izolirani incident. Riječ je o političkom sporu koji traje otprilike od **2005. godine**. Tada je vlast preuzela konzervativna stranka **Pravo i pravda (PiS)**, koju su predvodili blizanci **Lech i Jarosław Kaczyński**. PiS je tada vladao dvije godine, a nakon krize njegove vlasti vratila se stranka koju gost opisuje kao lijevo-liberalnu.

Ta se stranka danas zove **Građanska koalicija**, a ranije je nosila ime **Građanska platforma** Donalda Tuska. Pripada grupaciji **Europske pučke stranke** i formalno bi trebala biti pučka konzervativna stranka. Andrijanić ipak tvrdi da sve u njezinu programu i političkoj praksi pokazuje da se kreće prema lijevom centru.

Gost zatim prolazi kroz kronologiju:
- **2005.–2007.**: prva vlada PiS-a,
- **2007.–2015.**: dva mandata Građanske koalicije, tijekom kojih Tusk u jednom trenutku odlazi na, kako kaže, „sinekuru“ u Europsku uniju,
- **2015.–2023.**: PiS ponovno na vlasti dva mandata. Prema Andrijaniću, tada kreće duboka politička i gospodarska transformacija Poljske,
- **2023.**: Tusk se vraća na vlast.
sections.subtitle_en: Twenty Years of War Between Two Camps: From 2005 to Today
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran Andrijanić explains the beginning of the conflict in 2005
sections.content_en:
Andrijanić explains that the current crisis is not an isolated incident. It is a political dispute that has been going on approximately since **2005**. At that time, power was taken over by the conservative party **Law and Justice (PiS)**, led by the twins **Lech and Jarosław Kaczyński**. PiS then ruled for two years, and after the crisis of its government, the party that the guest describes as left-liberal returned.

That party is today called the **Civic Coalition**, and previously bore the name **Civic Platform** of Donald Tusk. It belongs to the **European People's Party** group and formally should be a popular conservative party. Andrijanić nevertheless claims that everything in its program and political practice shows that it is moving toward the center-left.

The guest then goes through the chronology:
- **2005–2007**: the first PiS government,
- **2007–2015**: two mandates of the Civic Coalition, during which Tusk at one point leaves for, as he says, a “sinecure” in the European Union,
- **2015–2023**: PiS again in power for two mandates. According to Andrijanić, a deep political and economic transformation of Poland began then,
- **2023**: Tusk returns to power.

sections.subtitle: Dvije frakcije Solidarnosti i dva pogleda na Treću republiku
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić pojašnjava da oba suprotstavljena tabora potječu iz Solidarnosti
sections.content:
Andrijanić naglašava da **oba tabora potječu iz pokreta Solidarnost**. Ni u jednoj od dviju glavnih stranaka nema postkomunista, osim u marginalnom smislu. Iznimka je, kako kaže, to što Tusk već dulje vrijeme surađuje s postkomunističkim snagama.

Prvu frakciju predvode braća Kaczyński. Gost je opisuje kao bližu konzervativnim vrijednostima i nezadovoljnu razvojem nakon pada komunizma. Taj tabor nije zadovoljan pretvorbom i transformacijom, a ponajviše procesom **lustracije**, koja se iz njegove perspektive uopće nije dogodila. Andrijanić podsjeća da je i sam pisao kako Poljska, suprotno raširenim predodžbama u Hrvatskoj i drugdje u Europi, **nije lustrirana**.

Druga frakcija je Građanska koalicija, koju gost naziva lijevim krilom Solidarnosti. Napominje da je i Tusk bio u Solidarnosti. Prema Andrijaniću, Tusk je s vremenom počeo surađivati s postkomunističkim strukturama koje su ostale u društvu i graditi sustav u koji su one bile uključene.

Tu gost vidi temeljnu razliku u shvaćanju **Treće republike**. Riječ je o poljskoj državi nastaloj nakon okruglog stola 1989. i djelomično slobodnih izbora koji su uslijedili. Pitanje je je li Treća republika:
- **potpuno ispunjenje** slobodarskih i demokratskih ideala Solidarnosti, kako je vidi Tuskov tabor, ili
- **kompromitacija i prodaja tih ideala**, kako je vide konzervativci. U unutarnjoj politici to pripisuju koaliranju s postkomunistima, a u vanjskoj vezivanju uz strana središta moći, ponajprije **Berlin**, s kojim je Tusk po Andrijanićevim riječima iznimno povezan, a zatim i Bruxelles.
sections.subtitle_en: Two Factions of Solidarity and Two Views on the Third Republic
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić clarifies that both opposing camps originate from Solidarity
sections.content_en:
Andrijanić emphasizes that **both camps originate from the Solidarity movement**. In neither of the two main parties are there post-communists, except in a marginal sense. The exception is, as he says, that Tusk has been cooperating with post-communist forces for a long time.

The first faction is led by the Kaczyński brothers. The guest describes it as closer to conservative values and dissatisfied with the development after the fall of communism. That camp is not satisfied with the privatization and transformation, and most of all with the process of **lustration**, which from its perspective did not happen at all. Andrijanić recalls that he himself wrote that Poland, contrary to widespread perceptions in Croatia and elsewhere in Europe, **was not lustrated**.

The second faction is the Civic Coalition, which the guest calls the left wing of Solidarity. He notes that Tusk was also in Solidarity. According to Andrijanić, over time Tusk began to cooperate with the post-communist structures that remained in society and to build a system in which they were included.

Here the guest sees the fundamental difference in the understanding of the **Third Republic**. It refers to the Polish state created after the 1989 round table and the partially free elections that followed. The question is whether the Third Republic is:
- **the complete fulfillment** of the libertarian and democratic ideals of Solidarity, as Tusk's camp sees it, or
- **a compromise and sell-out of those ideals**, as conservatives see it. In domestic policy they attribute this to coalition with post-communists, and in foreign policy to tying oneself to foreign centers of power, primarily **Berlin**, with which Tusk is, according to Andrijanić's words, exceptionally connected, and then also Brussels.

sections.subtitle: Kaczyński i Tusk: intelektualac iz Piłsudskijeve tradicije i gdanjski liberal
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić opisuje Jarosława Kaczyńskog kao vrhunskog intelektualca
sections.content:
Prema Andrijaniću, borba traje petnaestak do dvadesetak godina i ima dvije glavne ličnosti. Prva je **Jarosław Kaczyński**, sadašnji čelnik Prava i pravde. Gost podsjeća i na važnost njegova brata, predsjednika **Lecha Kaczyńskog**, koji je poginuo u avionskoj nesreći u **Smolensku 2010. godine**. Mnogi, kako kaže, smatraju da su okolnosti nesreće bile sumnjive. Tu tragediju opisuje kao prijelomnu točku poljske politike.

Jarosława Kaczyńskog gost opisuje kao **vrhunskog intelektualca** koji je ponikao iz lijeve državotvorne tradicije **Józefa Piłsudskog**. Piłsudski je bio na čelu poljske države između dvaju svjetskih ratova, a kao mladić bio je član Poljske socijalističke stranke. Andrijanić ističe da je to bila socijaldemokracija koja je u Poljskoj od početka bila državotvorna. Kaczyński je kroz Pravo i pravdu s vremenom postajao sve konzervativniji, što gost naziva vrlo zanimljivom situacijom.

Druga presudna ličnost je **Donald Tusk**, koji dolazi iz kružoka **gdanjskih liberala** povezanih sa Solidarnošću. Andrijanić ga opisuje kao tipičnog predstavnika europske liberalne demokracije, u vrlo dobrim odnosima s europskim establišmentom i središtima moći. Kao dokaz navodi Tuskovu „sinekuru“ u Bruxellesu.
sections.subtitle_en: Kaczyński and Tusk: An Intellectual from Piłsudski's Tradition and a Gdańsk Liberal
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić describes Jarosław Kaczyński as a top intellectual
sections.content_en:
According to Andrijanić, the struggle has lasted fifteen to twenty years and has two main figures. The first is **Jarosław Kaczyński**, the current leader of Law and Justice. The guest also recalls the importance of his brother, President **Lech Kaczyński**, who died in the plane crash in **Smolensk in 2010**. Many, as he says, consider the circumstances of the accident to have been suspicious. He describes that tragedy as a turning point in Polish politics.

The guest describes Jarosław Kaczyński as a **top intellectual** who emerged from the leftist state-building tradition of **Józef Piłsudski**. Piłsudski was at the head of the Polish state between the two world wars, and as a young man was a member of the Polish Socialist Party. Andrijanić points out that this was a social democracy that in Poland was state-building from the beginning. Through Law and Justice, Kaczyński became increasingly conservative over time, which the guest calls a very interesting situation.

The second crucial figure is **Donald Tusk**, who comes from the circle of **Gdańsk liberals** associated with Solidarity. Andrijanić describes him as a typical representative of European liberal democracy, on very good terms with the European establishment and centers of power. As proof, he cites Tusk's “sinecure” in Brussels.

sections.subtitle: Nawrocki: „dečko iz kvarta“ koji je pomeo favorita
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić opisuje Karola Nawrockog kao čovjeka iz radničkog okruženja
sections.content:
Treći čimbenik u igri je predsjednik **Karol Nawrocki**. U politiku je ušao na predsjedničkim izborima **2025.**, nakon parlamentarnih izbora na kojima je vlast osvojila lijevo-liberalna koalicija. Njegov glavni protukandidat bio je gradonačelnik Varšave **Rafał Trzaskowski**, kojemu su to bili drugi predsjednički izbori. Prve je izgubio 2020. od **Andrzeja Dude**. Andrijanić ga opisuje kao mladog čovjeka povezanog s lijevo-liberalnim krugovima u inozemstvu, koje naziva čak „šoroševskima“, i smatra ga možda povezanijim od samog Tuska.

Nawrocki je u tom trenutku bio na čelu **Nacionalnog instituta za sjećanje**. Gost tu ustanovu opisuje kao vrlo specifičnu u srednjoeuropskom kontekstu, jer se bavi ponajprije lustracijom poljskog društva. Prije toga Nawrocki je vodio **Muzej Drugoga svjetskog rata u Gdanjsku**, a po struci je doktor povijesti. Andrijanić ga opisuje kao „dečka iz kvarta“, čovjeka iz radničkog okruženja i nogometnog navijača, koji je akademsku i intelektualnu karijeru izgradio vlastitim radom.

Gost ističe da se u konzervativnim krugovima dugo raspravljalo koga postaviti protiv Trzaskowskog, jer se činilo da će Trzaskowski lako pobijediti. Da se to dogodilo, upozorava Andrijanić, **Tusk bi zatvorio cijeli politički sustav** i radio s Poljskom što bi htio. Kao znak iste tendencije navodi i sadašnja zbivanja oko Ustavnog suda. Nawrocki je, međutim, izletio „praktički niotkuda“ i zahvaljujući specifičnoj karizmi u kratkom vremenu pomeo Trzaskowskog.

Formalno je bio **nezavisni kandidat**, ali de facto kandidat PiS-a, koji mu je organizirao i financirao kampanju. Andrijanić to vidi kao još jedan lukav potez Jarosława Kaczyńskog, koji je osjetio da treba izvanstranačkog kandidata. Nawrocki je sada osovina oko koje se vrti dinamika desne konzervativne scene. Uslijedila je priča o njegovu mandatu, vetima na zakone koje predlaže parlament i, naravno, o Ustavnom sudu.

sections.subtitle_en: Nawrocki: A “Guy from the Neighborhood” Who Swept the Favorite
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić describes Karol Nawrocki as a man from a working-class background
sections.content_en:
The third factor in play is President **Karol Nawrocki**. He entered politics in the presidential elections of **2025**, after the parliamentary elections in which the left-liberal coalition won power. His main opponent was the Mayor of Warsaw, **Rafał Trzaskowski**, for whom these were his second presidential elections. He lost the first in 2020 to **Andrzej Duda**. Andrijanić describes him as a young man connected with left-liberal circles abroad, which he even calls “Soros-like”, and considers him perhaps more connected than Tusk himself.

At that moment, Nawrocki was at the head of the **Institute of National Remembrance**. The guest describes this institution as very specific in the Central European context, because it deals primarily with the lustration of Polish society. Before that, Nawrocki headed the **Museum of the Second World War in Gdańsk**, and by profession he is a doctor of history. Andrijanić describes him as a “guy from the neighborhood”, a man from a working-class background and a soccer fan, who built an academic and intellectual career through his own work.

The guest points out that in conservative circles there was a long debate about whom to put up against Trzaskowski, because it seemed that Trzaskowski would win easily. Had that happened, Andrijanić warns, **Tusk would have closed the entire political system** and done whatever he wanted with Poland. As a sign of the same tendency, he also cites current events surrounding the Constitutional Court. Nawrocki, however, burst out “practically from nowhere” and, thanks to a specific charisma, swept Trzaskowski in a short time.

Formally he was an **independent candidate**, but de facto the candidate of PiS, which organized and financed his campaign. Andrijanić sees this as another shrewd move by Jarosław Kaczyński, who sensed that an extra-party candidate was needed. Nawrocki is now the axis around which the dynamics of the right-wing conservative scene revolve. A story followed about his mandate, vetoes on laws proposed by the parliament, and, of course, about the Constitutional Court.
entities_en: Museum of the Second World War in Gdańsk

sections.subtitle: Desno od PiS-a: Konfederacija i Konfederacija poljske krune
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić govori o strankama desno od PiS-a i njihovoj potpori Nawrockom
sections.content:
Na trenutak gost zastaje i pita voditeljicu je li otišao previše u širinu. Ona ga potiče da slobodno nastavi. Andrijanić zatim objašnjava da na poljskoj sceni **desno od PiS-a** postoje dvije važne grupacije: **Konfederacija** i **Konfederacija poljske krune**. Zajedno trenutačno imaju između **20 i 25 posto glasova**.

Ključno je, ističe gost, da je Nawrocki bio i njihov kandidat. Probio je stranačke okvire, a bez toga, prema Andrijaniću, ne bi mogao pobijediti. Upravo zato što je blizak i krugovima desnije od PiS-a, uspio je objediniti širu konzervativnu i domoljubnu scenu.
sections.subtitle_en: To the Right of PiS: Confederation and the Confederation of the Polish Crown
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić speaks about the parties to the right of PiS and their support for Nawrocki
sections.content_en:
For a moment the guest pauses and asks the host whether he has broadened the topic too much. She encourages him to feel free to continue. Andrijanić then explains that on the Polish scene **to the right of PiS** there are two important groupings: **Confederation** and the **Confederation of the Polish Crown**. Together they currently have between **20 and 25 percent of the votes**.

Crucially, the guest points out, Nawrocki was also their candidate. He broke through party frameworks, and without that, according to Andrijanić, he would not have been able to win. Precisely because he is close to circles further to the right of PiS, he managed to unite the broader conservative and patriotic scene.

sections.subtitle: Suverenisti protiv globalista: Tusk kao „autentični antiamerikanac“
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić potvrđuje da je riječ o sukobu suverenista i globalista
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita je li riječ o borbi između **suverenista i globalista**. Andrijanić to bez zadrške potvrđuje. Dodaje da obje koncepcije smatra legitimnima, jer svatko ima svoju viziju vlastite države.

Prema gostu, intelektualni krug oko Tuska smatra da je jedina izvjesna budućnost Poljske u tome da se drži Njemačke i s njom ide bilo kamo, „pa ako treba i u propast“. To se, kaže, prikriva kao proeuropska orijentacija, a PiS i ostale konzervativne snage prikazuju se kao eurofobične. Andrijanić to smatra potpuno netočnim. U Poljskoj, tvrdi, nema ozbiljne eurofobične snage, osim eventualno Konfederacije poljske krune i **Grzegorza Brauna**. Ni oni, koliko je njemu poznato, nikada nisu otvoreno rekli da Poljska treba izaći iz Unije. **Polexit** je za njega strašilo kojim se Tusk koristi, a tvrdnje da konzervativci žele izaći iz Europe naziva „glupostima“.

Glavni prigovor konzervativaca Tusku jest da cijeli koncept Poljske gradi na privrženosti Njemačkoj i „takozvanim europskim idealima“:
- ako Njemačka ide u centralizaciju Unije, i Tusk ide u centralizaciju,
- ako se Njemačka distancira od Amerike, i Tusk se distancira od Amerike.

Andrijanić Tuska opisuje kao možda **jedinog autentično antiameričkog lidera** u Europskoj uniji, zajedno s ministrom vanjskih poslova **Radosławom Sikorskim**. Kaže da je to apsurdno i da Poljska zbog toga ima velik problem.

Nasuprot tome stoji **Nawrocki**, koji dolazi iz tradicije klasičnog poljskog domoljublja. Gost smatra da on objedinjuje najbolje iz poljske državotvorne misli, od **Romana Dmowskog** i **Józefa Piłsudskog** do **Ivana Pavla II.**, odnosno Karola Wojtyłe. Nawrocki je, kao zanimljivost navodi Andrijanić, dobio ime upravo po njemu i smatra ga najvažnijim Poljakom. Njegova je pozicija obojena katoličkim identitetom, ali duboko ukorijenjena u europsku tradiciju, od koje ne bježi.

Razlike se, zaključuje gost, vide u odnosu prema Središnjoj europskoj banci, euru, NATO-u i Europskoj uniji. Tusk je vjerno slijedio smjer centralizacije Unije prema zamislima Berlina i Pariza, iako je taj proces sada pomalo zastao. Nawrocki je prema tome bio skeptičan.
sections.subtitle_en: Sovereignists Against Globalists: Tusk as an “Authentic Anti-American”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić confirms that this is a conflict between sovereignists and globalists
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether this is a struggle between **sovereignists and globalists**. Andrijanić confirms this without hesitation. He adds that he considers both concepts legitimate, because everyone has their own vision of their state.

According to the guest, the intellectual circle around Tusk believes that the only certain future for Poland is to stick with Germany and go anywhere with it, “even into ruin if necessary”. This, he says, is masked as a pro-European orientation, while PiS and other conservative forces are portrayed as Europhobic. Andrijanić considers this completely incorrect. In Poland, he claims, there is no serious Europhobic force, except possibly the Confederation of the Polish Crown and **Grzegorz Braun**. Even they, as far as he knows, have never openly said that Poland should leave the Union. For him, **Polexit** is a bogeyman used by Tusk, and he calls claims that conservatives want to leave Europe “stupidities”.

The main conservative grievance against Tusk is that he builds the entire concept of Poland on devotion to Germany and “so-called European ideals”:
- if Germany moves toward centralization of the Union, Tusk also moves toward centralization,
- if Germany distances itself from America, Tusk also distances himself from America.

Andrijanić describes Tusk as perhaps **the only authentically anti-American leader** in the European Union, together with Foreign Minister **Radosław Sikorski**. He says that this is absurd and that Poland has a big problem because of it.

Opposite this stands **Nawrocki**, who comes from the tradition of classic Polish patriotism. The guest considers that he unites the best of Polish state-building thought, from **Roman Dmowski** and **Józef Piłsudski** to **John Paul II**, namely Karol Wojtyła. Nawrocki, as Andrijanić notes as an interesting detail, was named precisely after him and considers him the most important Pole. His position is colored by a Catholic identity, but deeply rooted in European tradition, from which he does not run away.

The differences, the guest concludes, are visible in the attitude toward the European Central Bank, the euro, NATO, and the European Union. Tusk faithfully followed the course of centralization of the Union according to the ideas of Berlin and Paris, although that process has now somewhat stalled. Nawrocki was skeptical towards that.

sections.subtitle: Zašto je Tusk „politički zaljubljen“ u Njemačku: stipendije, Merkel i mediji
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić objašnjava njemački soft power i stipendije za aktiviste Solidarnosti
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita zašto je Tusk toliko, kako kaže, „politički zaljubljen“ u Njemačku. Andrijanić odgovara da je to fascinantna stvar koja ni njemu isprva nije bila jasna. Polazište vidi u Tuskovu podrijetlu: Tusk je iz **Gdanjska**, a tamošnji liberalni kružok uvijek je bio vezan uz Njemačku.

Posebno ga je zanimalo odakle takva privrženost nakon Drugoga svjetskog rata i traume koju su Poljaci doživjeli s Nijemcima. Odgovor je dobio u razgovorima s upućenim ljudima. Njemačka je vrlo jaka u **soft poweru**, kulturno-intelektualnoj diplomaciji. Početkom devedesetih velik broj intelektualaca, političkih i društvenih djelatnika i aktivista iz Solidarnosti dobivao je **stipendije raznih njemačkih zaklada**. Tako se, prema gostu, stvorio krug političara privrženih njemačkom pogledu na Poljsku, Europu i svijet. Tusk je klasičan predstavnik tog kruga.

Andrijanić Tuska naziva **„političkim djetetom Angele Merkel“**, koja mu je od početka bila mentorica. Dodaje da je Merkel bila politička mentorica i **Aleksandru Vučiću**. Voditeljica primjećuje: „Pa znamo kako je Vučić završio.“ Gost odgovara da ostaje vidjeti hoće li i Tusk tako završiti.

Drugi stup njemačkog utjecaja gost vidi u **vlasništvu nad poljskim medijima**, u kojem su Nijemci jako prisutni. Kao primjer navodi koncern **Axel Springer**, koji u Poljskoj ima nekoliko portala i tjednik **Newsweek**. Zbog toga je, zaključuje Andrijanić, svaki političar koji je slijedio njemački kurs uvijek imao snažno medijsko pokriće, kao što ga Tusk ima i danas.
sections.subtitle_en: Why Tusk is “Politically in Love” with Germany: Scholarships, Merkel, and Media
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić explains German soft power and scholarships for Solidarity activists
sections.content_en:
The host asks why Tusk is so, as she says, “politically in love” with Germany. Andrijanić answers that this is a fascinating thing that was not clear to him either at first. He sees the starting point in Tusk's origin: Tusk is from **Gdańsk**, and the local liberal circle was always tied to Germany.

He was especially interested in where such devotion came from after the Second World War and the trauma that Poles experienced with the Germans. He received the answer in conversations with well-informed people. Germany is very strong in **soft power**, cultural-intellectual diplomacy. At the beginning of the nineties, a large number of intellectuals, political and social figures, and activists from Solidarity received **scholarships from various German foundations**. Thus, according to the guest, a circle of politicians devoted to the German view of Poland, Europe, and the world was created. Tusk is a classic representative of that circle.

Andrijanić calls Tusk **“the political child of Angela Merkel”**, who was his mentor from the beginning. He adds that Merkel was also a political mentor to **Aleksandar Vučić**. The host remarks: “Well, we know how Vučić ended up.” The guest replies that it remains to be seen whether Tusk will end up like that as well.

The guest sees the second pillar of German influence in **ownership of the Polish media**, in which the Germans are very present. As an example, he cites the **Axel Springer** concern, which in Poland owns several portals and the weekly **Newsweek**. Because of this, Andrijanić concludes, every politician who followed the German course always had strong media coverage, just as Tusk has today.

sections.subtitle: „Četvrti Reich“ i Tuskov povratak iz Bruxellesa
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić tumači Kaczyńskijev izraz „Četvrti Reich“
sections.content:
Voditeljica postavlja provokativno pitanje. Najavljuje da će možda biti gruba, ali dodaje da „još uvijek valjda živimo u slobodnom svijetu“. Zanima je događa li se ono što je 1939. započeo „čovjek s brčićima“ sada u Poljskoj na sofisticiraniji način, kroz meku, medijsku i političku moć.

Andrijanić odgovara da nije nimalo gruba, nego vrlo precizna. Podsjeća da je **Jarosław Kaczyński** ono što Njemačka radi u Europskoj uniji nazvao **„Četvrtim Reichom“**. Time je opisao centralizaciju Unije i usmjeravanje svih kanala političke i društvene moći prema Berlinu. Kaczyński je to rekao 2020. ili 2021., no gost prenosi da mu je **Ivica Šola** u razgovoru rekao kako je on taj termin za Europsku uniju upotrijebio još 2017. ili 2018. Andrijanić naglašava da ne želi banalizirati stvari, ali smatra da je sve što se godinama događa u Poljskoj posljedica tendencije Berlina da kontrolira situaciju u toj zemlji.

U tom kontekstu gost iznosi tezu o Tuskovu povratku. Tusk je bio na čelu Vijeća u Bruxellesu, a Andrijanić usput napominje da ljudi naziv te institucije stalno miješaju. Zatim je postao šef Europske pučke stranke i činilo se da će ostati u Bruxellesu. Ipak se 2020. ili 2021. vratio u Poljsku. Prema uobičajenoj interpretaciji koju gost prenosi, **Nijemci su ga nagovorili da se vrati**. Kružili su i snimljeni razgovori iz kojih je, kaže, bilo jasno da mu se uopće nije vraćalo.

Andrijanić Tuska opisuje kao kompetentnog političara u makijavelističkom smislu: „nevjerojatnog manipulanta“, „dijabolično inteligentnog“ i elokventnog. Vlast je, prema njemu, preuzeo na vrlo manipulativan način, ali je pobijedio. Gost ponavlja da je poljska stvarnost puno složenija. Ipak, sukob svodi na ovu formulu: **poljska politika koja ostvaruje njemačke interese protiv poljskog suverenizma koji tome pokušava kontrirati**.
sections.subtitle_en: The “Fourth Reich” and Tusk's Return from Brussels
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić interprets Kaczyński's expression “Fourth Reich”
sections.content_en:
The host asks a provocative question. She announces that she might be harsh, but adds that “we still probably live in a free world”. She is interested in whether what the “man with the little mustache” started in 1939 is now happening in Poland in a more sophisticated way, through soft, media, and political power.

Andrijanić replies that she is not harsh at all, but very precise. He recalls that **Jarosław Kaczyński** called what Germany is doing in the European Union the **“Fourth Reich”**. By that he described the centralization of the Union and the directing of all channels of political and social power toward Berlin. Kaczyński said this in 2020 or 2021, but the guest conveys that **Ivica Šola** told him in conversation that he used that term for the European Union as early as 2017 or 2018. Andrijanić emphasizes that he does not want to trivialize things, but considers that everything that has been happening in Poland for years is the consequence of Berlin's tendency to control the situation in that country.

In that context, the guest presents a thesis about Tusk's return. Tusk was at the head of the Council in Brussels, and Andrijanić notes in passing that people constantly mix up the name of that institution. Then he became the head of the European People's Party and it seemed he would stay in Brussels. Nevertheless, in 2020 or 2021 he returned to Poland. According to the usual interpretation conveyed by the guest, **the Germans persuaded him to return**. Recorded conversations also circulated from which, he says, it was clear that he did not feel like returning at all.

Andrijanić describes Tusk as a competent politician in a Machiavellian sense: an “unbelievable manipulator”, “diabolically intelligent”, and eloquent. He took power, according to him, in a very manipulative way, but he won. The guest repeats that Polish reality is much more complex. Nevertheless, he reduces the conflict to this formula: **Polish politics realizing German interests against Polish sovereignism trying to counter that**.

sections.subtitle: Gospodarska kriza iza fasade: deficit, nezaposlenost i pad Krakova
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić govori o deficitu i lošijoj kvaliteti života u Poljskoj
sections.content:
Andrijanić tvrdi da je jedan od glavnih zadataka Donalda Tuska bio da gospodarsko, političko i vojno „čudo“ iz osam godina vlasti PiS-a „spusti na zemlju“. Voditeljica se iznenađeno pita zar to radi kao premijer Poljske. Gost potvrđuje da se upravo to događa.

Njemački soft power vidi i u hrvatskim medijima. Svaki put kad Tusk, kako kaže, napravi neku glupost, u hrvatskim medijima čita članke prepisane iz **Deutsche Wellea** ili drugih izvora o tome kako je Poljska ekonomski savršena. Prema Andrijaniću, stvarnost je drukčija:
- BDP se još drži, ali je **deficit ogroman**,
- proračunski deficit za **2027.** mjeri se u iznosu od oko **60 milijardi eura**, što je više od **7 posto BDP-a**,
- po tom pokazatelju Poljska je, smatra gost, druga u Europi, iza Rumunjske ili slično,
- **nezaposlenost raste**,
- ljudi nakon dugo vremena osjećaju da žive lošije nego prije.

Kao simptom navodi **Krakov**, koji opisuje kao vrlo važan grad i za Hrvate, jer su nekad bili dio istog kraljevstva. Građani su ondje organizirali **referendum za opoziv** gradonačelnika iz Građanske koalicije, Michalskog. Andrijanić naglašava da to nije bila stranačka inicijativa PiS-a, kako ju je Tusk pokušavao prikazati. Gradonačelnik je vladao godinu i pol do dvije i, prema gostu, „rasturio Krakov“.

Na izborima koji su uslijedili Tuskovu kandidatkinju deklasirao je nezavisni kandidat Giballa. Gost priznaje da se ne može sjetiti imena kandidatkinje Građanske koalicije i dodaje da je „toliko nevažna da joj je čak i ime zaboravio“. Gubitak Krakova naziva velikim porazom Građanske koalicije. Kao glavni razlog glasanja protiv njezina kandidata ankete navode **kvalitetu života**, koja je jednostavno lošija.
sections.subtitle_en: Economic Crisis Behind the Facade: Deficit, Unemployment, and the Fall of Kraków
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić speaks about the deficit and poorer quality of life in Poland
sections.content_en:
Andrijanić claims that one of Donald Tusk's main tasks was to “bring down to earth” the economic, political, and military “miracle” from the eight years of PiS rule. The host wonders in surprise whether he is doing that as Prime Minister of Poland. The guest confirms that this is precisely what is happening.

He also sees German soft power in Croatian media. Every time Tusk, as he says, does something stupid, in Croatian media he reads articles copied from **Deutsche Welle** or other sources about how Poland is economically perfect. According to Andrijanić, reality is different:
- GDP is still holding up, but the **deficit is huge**,
- the budget deficit for **2027** is measured at an amount of around **60 billion euros**, which is more than **7 percent of GDP**,
- by that indicator Poland is, the guest considers, second in Europe, behind Romania or similar,
- **unemployment is rising**,
- people after a long time feel that they live worse than before.

As a symptom, he cites **Kraków**, which he describes as a very important city for Croats as well, because they were once part of the same kingdom. Citizens there organized a **recall referendum** for the mayor from the Civic Coalition, Michalski. Andrijanić emphasizes that this was not a party initiative of PiS, as Tusk tried to portray it. The mayor ruled for a year and a half to two years and, according to the guest, “wrecked Kraków”.

In the elections that followed, Tusk's candidate was trounced by the independent candidate Giballa. The guest admits that he cannot remember the name of the Civic Coalition candidate and adds that she is “so unimportant that I even forgot her name”. He calls the loss of Kraków a major defeat for the Civic Coalition. As the main reason for voting against its candidate, polls cite **quality of life**, which is simply worse.

sections.subtitle: Pokopani „game changer“: središnji prometni čvor između Varšave i Łódźa
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić objašnjava projekt središnjeg prometnog čvora i odustajanje od njega
sections.content:
Prema Andrijaniću, Tusk je imao za cilj usporiti gospodarski rast Poljske. Ne uništiti je, jer bi to bilo besmisleno, ali usporiti rast i odustati od velikih investicija. Kao ključan primjer navodi **središnji prometni čvor**.

To je trebalo biti glavno središte za sav zrakoplovni robni promet sa smjera istoka, ponajprije iz **Kine**. Čvor je bio planiran između **Łódźa i Varšave**, u samom središtu Poljske, koje je prema gostu manje-više i središte tog dijela Europe. Ondje bi se slijevala roba iz Kine i s istoka i odande se prosljeđivala dalje. Andrijanić podsjeća da monopol nad takvim kargo prometom, u kojem se vrte veliki novci i plaćaju takse, trenutačno imaju **Nijemci**.

Od projekta se, prema gostu, potpuno odustalo i o njemu se uopće ne govori. Tusk je isprva tvrdio da je projekt preambiciozan i da će ga usporiti. Da je PiS ostao na vlasti, smatra Andrijanić, projekt bi bio ostvaren. Naziva ga ekonomskim **„game changerom“** od kojeg ne bi profitirala samo Poljska, nego cijela središnja Europa, uključujući Hrvatsku.

Gost zaključuje oštrom ocjenom: Tusk državu koja je počela pokazivati ozbiljne ambicije u svakom smislu vraća u **„nekakav kolonijalni status“**. To je, prema njemu, Tuskova glavna zadaća.
sections.subtitle_en: Buried “Game Changer”: Central Transport Hub Between Warsaw and Łódź
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić explains the central transport hub project and its abandonment
sections.content_en:
According to Andrijanić, Tusk aimed to slow down Poland's economic growth. Not to destroy it, because that would be pointless, but to slow down growth and abandon major investments. As a key example he cites the **central transport hub**.

That was supposed to be the main center for all air cargo transport from the direction of the east, primarily from **China**. The hub was planned between **Łódź and Warsaw**, in the very center of Poland, which according to the guest is more or less also the center of that part of Europe. Goods from China and the east would flow there and be forwarded onward from there. Andrijanić recalls that the monopoly over such cargo traffic, in which large amounts of money circulate and duties are paid, is currently held by the **Germans**.

The project, according to the guest, was completely abandoned and is not talked about at all. Tusk initially claimed that the project was overly ambitious and that he would slow it down. Had PiS stayed in power, Andrijanić considers, the project would have been realized. He calls it an economic **“game changer”** from which not only Poland would have profited, but the whole of Central Europe, including Croatia.

The guest concludes with a sharp assessment: Tusk is returning a country that had begun to show serious ambitions in every sense to **“some kind of colonial status”**. That is, according to him, Tusk's main task.

sections.subtitle: Kako je pobjednik ostao bez vlasti: Tuskova koalicija s postkomunistima i Trećim putem
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić objašnjava kako je Tusk formirao koaliciju unatoč pobjedi PiS-a
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita jesu li Poljaci to shvatili, s obzirom na to da je Tusk izabran na izborima. Odmah se ispravlja da on nije izabran izravno, nego se izravno bira predsjednik. Andrijanić pojašnjava da je na parlamentarnim izborima **najviše glasova dobio PiS**, ali nije mogao formirati koaliciju.

To je uspjelo Tusku, koji je koaliciju sklopio s nekoliko stranaka. Među njima je i postkomunistička **Nova ljevica** **Włodzimierza Czarzastog**, koji je danas maršalek Sejma, odnosno predsjednik donjeg doma parlamenta. Gost ga naziva klasičnim komunistom, „starom komunjerom“, i dodaje da se i sam tako opisuje. Voditeljica primjećuje da je „barem priznao“. Prema Andrijaniću, to je još jedan dokaz da Tusk gradi sustav suradnje s postkomunističkim strukturama, koje u Trećoj republici nisu ostale nemoćne i obezglavljene.

Presudni su ipak bili glasovi koalicije **Treći put**. Nju su činile:
- stranka **Poljska 2050**, koju je vodio televizijski voditelj i celebrity **Szymon Hołownia**, koji se u jednom trenutku politički aktivirao,
- **PSL (Poljska narodna stranka)**, koju gost opisuje kao vrlo zanimljivu formaciju. Prema njegovim riječima, u komunizmu je bila jedina legalna stranka osim Komunističke partije. U sebi ima postkomunistički element, ali i stalno prisutan element narodnjaštva. Vjerojatno ima i najjaču logistiku na terenu, kroz mrežu načelnika općina i županija koja datira iz komunističkih vremena.

Zahvaljujući Trećem putu Tusk je mogao formirati vladu, ali ga je kasnije, kako kaže gost, „pojeo“: **Hołownia je uništen**. Čelnik PSL-a **Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz** danas je ministar obrane i potpredsjednik vlade. Mnoge su oči u sporu oko Ustavnog suda uprte upravo u njega, u nadi da bi se mogao okrenuti od Tuska. Andrijanić u to ne vjeruje.
sections.subtitle_en: How the Winner Was Left Without Power: Tusk's Coalition with Post-Communists and the Third Way
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić explains how Tusk formed a coalition despite the victory of PiS
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether Poles understood this, given that Tusk was elected in elections. She immediately corrects herself that he was not elected directly, but rather the president is elected directly. Andrijanić clarifies that in the parliamentary elections **PiS received the most votes**, but could not form a coalition.

This was achieved by Tusk, who formed a coalition with several parties. Among them is the post-communist **New Left** of **Włodzimierz Czarzasty**, who is today the Marshal of the Sejm, that is, the speaker of the lower house of parliament. The guest calls him a classic communist, an “old commie”, and adds that he describes himself that way as well. The host remarks that “at least he admitted it”. According to Andrijanić, this is another proof that Tusk is building a system of cooperation with post-communist structures, which in the Third Republic were not left powerless and headless.

Crucial, however, were the votes of the **Third Way** coalition. It consisted of:
- the party **Poland 2050**, led by television host and celebrity **Szymon Hołownia**, who became politically active at one point,
- the **PSL (Polish People's Party)**, which the guest describes as a very interesting formation. According to his words, under communism it was the only legal party besides the Communist Party. It has within itself a post-communist element, but also an ever-present element of agrarian populism. It probably also has the strongest logistics on the ground, through a network of commune and county mayors that dates back to communist times.

Thanks to the Third Way, Tusk was able to form a government, but later, as the guest says, he “ate” it: **Hołownia is ruined**. PSL leader **Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz** is today Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defense. Many eyes in the dispute over the Constitutional Court are directed precisely at him, in the hope that he might turn away from Tusk. Andrijanić does not believe in that.

sections.subtitle: Zašto je PiS izgubio i paradoks probuđene poljske samosvijesti
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić govori o samosvijesti i ambiciji koju je vladavina PiS-a probudila kod Poljaka
sections.content:
Kao glavni razlog poraza PiS-a Andrijanić navodi **medijsku mašineriju** koja stvara paralelnu stvarnost i djeluje na ljude. Priznaje i da PiS u osam godina nije vladao idealno te nabraja nekoliko pogrešaka:
- **odluka Ustavnog suda iz listopada 2020.** o zabrani eugeničkog pobačaja, nakon koje su uslijedili feministički i proabortivni prosvjedi. Gost ih opisuje kao politički kanalizirane i kaže da je na njima Tusk dobio. Mnogi to smatraju jednim od razloga poraza, ali Andrijanić se s tim ne slaže i taj val naziva balonom koji se s vremenom ispuhao,
- **pogreške u poreznim reformama**,
- **nedovoljno odlučna politika prema Europskoj uniji**, koja je PiS, kako kaže, ucjenjivala od samih početaka.

Ipak, presudnom smatra **manipulaciju**. Tusk, prema gostu, gradi karijeru na **polarizaciji** i nema konkretan program ni viziju. Podsjeća na poznatu Tuskovu izjavu: kad su mu prigovorili da nema viziju Poljske, odgovorio je da viziju imaju samo luđaci, a ne političari. Andrijanić ponavlja da je Tusk u makijavelističkom smislu vrlo kompetentan i zna manipulirati emocijama ljudi i usmjeravati ih.

U porazu PiS-a gost vidi i paradoks. On i ljudi s kojima razgovara u Poljskoj smatraju da je osam godina vlasti PiS-a stvorilo kod Poljaka **određenu samosvijest** i vratilo im ambiciju da budu autohtoni čimbenik barem u svom dijelu Europe. Voditeljica to sažima pitanjem: „Da mogu biti svoji?“ Andrijanić potvrđuje da im je vraćeno samopouzdanje i da je taj osjećaj ostao.

Paradoksalno je, zaključuje gost, da stranka koja je to probudila gubi izbore, a osjećaj ostaje. Velik dio današnjeg nezadovoljstva u Poljskoj tumači upravo tom probuđenom ambicijom koju Tusk ne ostvaruje. PiS je izgubio izbore, kaže Andrijanić, ali je odlučivala „jedna nijansa“.
sections.subtitle_en: Why PiS Lost and the Paradox of Awakened Polish Self-Awareness
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić speaks about the self-awareness and ambition that the rule of PiS awakened among Poles
sections.content_en:
As the main reason for PiS's defeat, Andrijanić cites the **media machinery** that creates a parallel reality and affects people. He also admits that PiS did not rule ideally during eight years and lists several mistakes:
- **the decision of the Constitutional Court from October 2020** banning eugenic abortion, after which feminist and pro-abortion protests followed. The guest describes them as politically channeled and says that Tusk gained on them. Many consider this one of the reasons for the defeat, but Andrijanić does not agree with that and calls that wave a balloon that deflated over time,
- **mistakes in tax reforms**,
- **an insufficiently decisive policy towards the European Union**, which, as he says, blackmailed PiS from the very beginning.

Nevertheless, he considers **manipulation** to be crucial. Tusk, according to the guest, builds his career on **polarization** and has neither a concrete program nor a vision. He recalls Tusk's well-known statement: when they criticized him for having no vision for Poland, he replied that only madmen have a vision, not politicians. Andrijanić repeats that Tusk is very competent in a Machiavellian sense and knows how to manipulate people's emotions and direct them.

In the defeat of PiS, the guest also sees a paradox. He and the people he talks to in Poland consider that eight years of PiS rule created **a certain self-awareness** among Poles and restored their ambition to be an indigenous factor at least in their part of Europe. The host summarizes this with the question: “That they can be their own masters?” Andrijanić confirms that their self-confidence was restored and that this feeling remained.

It is paradoxical, the guest concludes, that the party that awakened this loses the election, while the feeling remains. He interprets a large part of today's dissatisfaction in Poland precisely through that awakened ambition that Tusk does not fulfill. PiS lost the election, says Andrijanić, but it was decided by “a single nuance”.
