sections.subtitle: Kulturni rat i Ustavni sud kao ključ za „zatvaranje kruga”
sections.screenshot_description: Goran Andrijanić objašnjava zašto Tusk želi kontrolu nad Ustavnim sudom
sections.content:
Voditeljica podsjeća da joj je gost pri dogovaranju razgovora rekao kako se u Poljskoj vodi **idejni i kulturni rat**, pa ga pita o čemu je riječ. Goran Andrijanić potvrđuje da je riječ o kulturnom ratu. Na jednoj strani vidi globalistički koncept koji, kako kaže, uništava narodnu suverenost te sotonizira svako domoljublje i nacionalne interese. Na drugoj strani stoji pokušaj da se te vrijednosti sačuvaju.

Zatim prelazi na temu koja trenutačno potresa Poljsku, spor oko Ustavnog suda. Po njegovu mišljenju premijer Donald Tusk želi kontrolu nad tim sudom kako bi mogao **potpuno kontrolirati situaciju u državi**. Voditeljica ga podsjeća na izraz koji je ranije upotrijebio, da Tusk želi „zatvoriti krug”. Andrijanić to potvrđuje: zatvaranjem kruga Tusk bi predsjednika Karola Nawrockog na određeni način izbacio iz igre.

Gost upozorava da se već čuju glasovi ljudi koji su, kako kaže, sudjelovali u puču. Prema tim glasovima, ideja o opozivu predsjednika, o proglašavanju predsjednika nesposobnim ili o nekoj drugoj pravnoj odredbi koja bi ga uklonila s političke scene **uopće nije nemoguća**.
sections.subtitle_en: Culture War and the Constitutional Court as Key to “Closing the Circle”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran Andrijanić explains why Tusk wants control over the Constitutional Court
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that during the arrangement of the interview the guest told her that an **ideological and culture war** is being waged in Poland, so she asks him what it is about. Goran Andrijanić confirms that it is a culture war. On one side he sees a globalist concept that, as he says, destroys popular sovereignty and demonizes all patriotism and national interests. On the other side stands an attempt to preserve those values.

Then he moves to the topic currently shaking Poland, the dispute over the Constitutional Court. In his view, Prime Minister Donald Tusk wants control over that court in order to be able to **completely control the situation in the state**. The host reminds him of the expression he used earlier, that Tusk wants to “close the circle”. Andrijanić confirms this: by closing the circle, Tusk would in a certain way eliminate President Karol Nawrocki from the game.

The guest warns that the voices of people who, as he says, participated in the coup are already being heard. According to those voices, the idea of impeaching the president, declaring the president incapacitated, or some other legal provision that would remove him from the political scene **is not impossible at all**.

sections.subtitle: „Nasilna i bespravna intervencija”: je li to bio državni udar?
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić tvrdi da slanje policije u Ustavni sud smatra državnim udarom
sections.content:
Voditeljica izravno pita je li, po njegovu mišljenju, ipak riječ o pokušaju puča. Andrijanić odgovara da to ne zna drugačije nazvati. Za njega je to **neka forma državnog udara**. Objašnjava da državni udar može biti jači ili slabiji te da može pogoditi cijeli sustav odjednom ili samo jedan njegov dio. Ovo je, kaže, bila nasilna i bespravna intervencija usmjerena na Ustavni sud. Dodaje da nikome ne treba objašnjavati što Ustavni sud znači za svaki demokratski sustav. Kao državni udar izričito označava **slanje policije u državnu instituciju**.

Gost pritom ne idealizira nijednu stranu. Spor oko Ustavnog suda traje već **petnaest godina**, a i PiS-u i Građanskoj koaliciji može se prigovoriti da su radili mnogo dvojbenih i diskutabilnih stvari. Ipak, cijelo to vrijeme spor je ostajao u granicama političkoga i demokratskoga.

Andrijanić naglašava da politički sporovi sami po sebi nisu patologija. Kaže da se raduje kad vidi sporove u Hrvatskoj, jer to znači da različita središta moći nude vlastite vizije razvoja države, a ne bore se samo za preuzimanje nadzora nad njom. Na voditeljičino pitanje znači li to da „nismo svi ušutkani”, odgovara: **„Apsolutno”**. Važno je da ne mislimo svi jednako.

Slanje policije u Ustavni sud, međutim, prema njegovim riječima izašlo je izvan svih tih okvira. Za Tuskov potez **ne postoji nikakvo zakonsko opravdanje**. Vlada ne može navesti odredbu na koju bi se mogla pozvati.
sections.subtitle_en: “Violent and Unlawful Intervention”: Was It a Coup d'État?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić claims that he considers sending police to the Constitutional Court a coup d'état
sections.content_en:
The host asks directly whether, in his view, it is nevertheless an attempted coup. Andrijanić replies that he does not know how else to call it. For him it is **some form of coup d'état**. He explains that a coup d'état can be stronger or weaker and that it can affect the whole system at once or only a part of it. This, he says, was a violent and unlawful intervention directed at the Constitutional Court. He adds that no one needs to be told what the Constitutional Court means for every democratic system. As a coup d'état he explicitly designates **sending police into a state institution**.

The guest does not idealize either side in doing so. The dispute over the Constitutional Court has been going on for **fifteen years**, and both PiS and the Civic Coalition can be faulted for having done many dubious and debatable things. Nevertheless, all that time the dispute remained within political and democratic boundaries.

Andrijanić emphasizes that political disputes are not in themselves a pathology. He says that he is glad when he sees disputes in Croatia, because that means different centers of power are offering their own visions for the development of the state, and are not just fighting to take control over it. To the host's question whether that means “we are not all silenced”, he answers: **“Absolutely”**. It is important that we do not all think alike.

Sending police into the Constitutional Court, however, according to his words went beyond all those frameworks. For Tusk's move **there is no legal justification whatsoever**. The government cannot cite a provision to which it could refer.

sections.subtitle: Kronologija spora: prisega pred predsjednikom ili „pred bilo kim”
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić opisuje kako je Nawrocki odbio uzeti prisegu ustavnim sucima
sections.content:
Andrijanić zatim rekonstruira kako se došlo do eskalacije. Jedna od sutkinja, koja formalno još nije postala ustavna sutkinja jer nije položila prisegu pred predsjednikom, odlučila je **suspendirati predsjednika Ustavnog suda Bogdana Święczkowskog i potpredsjednika Sokołowskog**. Za takav potez, ističe gost, ne postoji nikakva zakonska kategorija ni ovlast. To priznaju i ljudi koji su Tuska godinama branili u sporu oko suda.

Potom objašnjava razliku prema postupku predsjednika Nawrockog, o čemu je, kako kaže, polemizirao i s kolegama iz Hrvatske. Kada je Nawrocki odbio uzeti prisegu sucima koje je izabrao parlament, djelovao je unutar određenog zakonskog okvira. Taj je okvir možda bio nategnut i kontroverzan, ali je postojao. Prema zakonu o ustavnim sucima, suci moraju položiti prisegu pred predsjednikom jer im u protivnom služba ne počinje.

Odbijanju je prethodio važan kontekst. Prema Andrijanićevim riječima, Tuskova je vlast nakon dolaska na vlast godinu i pol dana:

- izbacivala Ustavni sud iz igre i proglašavala ga nelegitimnim,
- nije objavljivala njegove odluke tamo gdje je to trebala,
- dovela je čak u pitanje hoće li ustavni suci dobivati plaće.

Kad je istekao mandat dovoljnom broju sudaca izabranih u vrijeme PiS-a, Tusk je nominirao njih šestero. Nawrocki je, prema gostovu prikazu, odgovorio: **„Ne, nećemo se tako igrati.”** Odlučio je uzeti prisegu od dvoje kandidata jer je zakonski minimum za donošenje odluka Ustavnog suda jedanaest sudaca. O ostalima nije donio konačnu odluku. To se dogodilo krajem ožujka i početkom travnja.

Ne čekajući predsjednikovu odluku, Tusk i njegovi suradnici, kako kaže Andrijanić, organizirali su „doista nakaradnu situaciju”. Tvrdili su da odredba o prisezi „pred predsjednikom” ne zahtijeva predsjednikovu nazočnost, nego da je dovoljno izgovoriti tekst prisege u bilo kojoj prigodi i pred bilo kim. Četvero kandidata tako je prisegnulo **među stupovima u prostorijama Sejma, bez predsjednika**. Odatle je nastala blokada.
sections.subtitle_en: Chronology of the Dispute: Oath Before the President or “Before Anyone”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić describes how Nawrocki refused to take the oath of constitutional judges
sections.content_en:
Andrijanić then reconstructs how the escalation came about. One of the judges, who formally had not yet become a constitutional judge because she had not taken the oath before the president, decided to **suspend Constitutional Court President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice President Sokołowski**. For such a move, the guest points out, there is no legal category or authority whatsoever. This is acknowledged even by people who have defended Tusk for years in the dispute over the court.

Then he explains the difference compared to the procedure of President Nawrocki, about which, as he says, he also debated with colleagues from Croatia. When Nawrocki refused to administer the oath to judges elected by the parliament, he acted within a certain legal framework. That framework may have been strained and controversial, but it existed. According to the law on constitutional judges, judges must take the oath before the president because otherwise their term of office does not begin.

The refusal was preceded by an important context. According to Andrijanić's words, Tusk's government, after coming to power for a year and a half:

- pushed the Constitutional Court out of the game and declared it illegitimate,
- did not publish its decisions where it was supposed to,
- even called into question whether constitutional judges would receive salaries.

When the mandate of a sufficient number of judges elected during PiS expired, Tusk nominated six of them. Nawrocki, according to the guest's depiction, answered: **“No, we will not play like that.”** He decided to administer the oath to two candidates because the legal minimum for Constitutional Court decisions is eleven judges. Regarding the others, he did not make a final decision. That happened at the end of March and beginning of April.

Without waiting for the president's decision, Tusk and his associates, as Andrijanić says, organized a “truly grotesque situation”. They claimed that the provision about taking the oath “before the president” does not require the president's presence, but rather that it is enough to recite the text of the oath on any occasion and before anyone. Four candidates thus took the oath **among the pillars in the premises of the Sejm, without the president**. That is where the impasse arose.

sections.subtitle: Slučaj Maciej Berek: premijerova desna ruka u Ustavnom sudu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o spornom imenovanju Macieja Bereka
sections.content:
Novi zaplet dogodio se, prema Andrijanićevim riječima, prije otprilike mjesec i pol do dva. Tusk je tada u Ustavni sud poslao **Macieja Bereka**, kojega gost opisuje kao „klasičnog stranačkog aktivista” i čovjeka koji je radio kao njegov asistent u Uredu premijera.

Andrijanić odbacuje tvrdnje da Berek nije političar. Tko radi u Uredu premijera i premijerova je desna ruka, kaže, nije običan birokrat u provincijskoj općini. Takav je čovjek političar koji ostvaruje političke ciljeve.

Sporan je bio i drugi uvjet. Za izbor ustavnog suca potrebno je **deset godina pravničke prakse**, a Berek to, prema gostovim riječima, nije mogao dokazati. Po obrazovanju jest pravnik, ali se izgleda od početka bavio politikom. Nawrocki je stoga odbio uzeti prisegu i od njega. Tako je nastala situacija u kojoj Tusk, kako kaže Andrijanić, „radi to što radi” i šalje policiju.
sections.subtitle_en: The Maciej Berek Case: The Prime Minister's Right-Hand Man in the Constitutional Court
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the controversial appointment of Maciej Berek
sections.content_en:
A new complication occurred, according to Andrijanić's words, about a month and a half to two months ago. Tusk then sent **Maciej Berek** to the Constitutional Court, whom the guest describes as a “classic party activist” and a man who worked as his assistant in the Chancellery of the Prime Minister.

Andrijanić rejects claims that Berek is not a politician. Whoever works in the Chancellery of the Prime Minister and is the prime minister's right-hand man, he says, is not an ordinary bureaucrat in a provincial municipality. Such a man is a politician who achieves political goals.

The second condition was also controversial. For election as a constitutional judge, **ten years of legal practice** are required, and Berek, according to the guest's words, could not prove that. By education he is a lawyer, but apparently he was involved in politics from the beginning. Nawrocki therefore refused to administer the oath to him as well. Thus a situation arose in which Tusk, as Andrijanić says, “does what he does” and sends the police.

sections.subtitle: Isti obrazac: televizija u likvidaciji i smjena državnog odvjetnika
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić prepričava kako je iz redakcije gledao prekid programa javne televizije TVP
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita je li slučajno što se akcija dogodila baš u petak navečer. Andrijanić odgovara odlučnim „ne”. Najprije naglašava da Tusk, po njegovoj ocjeni, od početka vladavine postupa na isti način: **ignorira zakone, demokratske običaje i zdrav razum**.

Kao primjer navodi preuzimanje javne televizije u prosincu 2023., otprilike mjesec dana nakon što je Tusk preuzeo vlast. Andrijanić je tada bio u redakciji i na jednom od ekrana pratio program TVP-a. U jednom trenutku program je prekinut. U zgradu tada nije ušla policija, nego **privatni zaštitari**, koji su doslovno preuzeli zgradu.

Objašnjava i pravni mehanizam. Postoji vijeće za medije bez kojega se ne mogu provoditi smjene, ali vlast je pronašla zakonsku rupu. Televiziju je tretirala kao bilo koje javno poduzeće i proglasila njezinu likvidaciju. Zato je cijeli javni medij i danas **formalno u likvidaciji**, iako normalno radi i troši ogromne novce. Sličan zahvat, kaže gost, dogodio se u tužiteljstvu, gdje je također iskorištena rupa u zakonu kako bi se smijenio glavni državni odvjetnik.

Andrijanić ističe i odabir trenutka. Preuzimanje televizije dogodilo se nekoliko dana uoči Božića, oko 20. prosinca, što smatra svjesno iskorištenim psihološkim momentom. Božić je kao novinar proveo u zgradama javne televizije, gdje su ljudi prosvjedovali. Badnju večer ipak je proveo s obitelji, dok su je neki njegovi kolege proveli ondje.
sections.subtitle_en: The Same Pattern: Television in Liquidation and Dismissal of the Public Prosecutor General
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić recounts how he watched the interruption of public television TVP broadcast from the newsroom
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether it is a coincidence that the action took place precisely on a Friday evening. Andrijanić replies with a decisive “no”. First he emphasizes that Tusk, according to his assessment, has been acting in the same way since the beginning of his rule: **he ignores laws, democratic customs, and common sense**.

As an example, he cites the takeover of public television in December 2023, approximately a month after Tusk took power. Andrijanić was in the newsroom at the time and was watching TVP's programming on one of the screens. At one point the broadcast was cut off. Police did not enter the building then, but **private security guards**, who literally took over the building.

He also explains the legal mechanism. There is a media council without which dismissals cannot be carried out, but the government found a legal loophole. It treated the television station like any public enterprise and declared its liquidation. That is why the entire public media outlet is still **formally in liquidation** today, even though it operates normally and spends huge amounts of money. A similar move, says the guest, occurred in the prosecutor's office, where a loophole in the law was also used to replace the Public Prosecutor General.

Andrijanić also highlights the choice of timing. The takeover of the television occurred a few days before Christmas, around December 20, which he considers a consciously exploited psychological moment. As a journalist he spent Christmas in the buildings of public television, where people were protesting. Christmas Eve he nevertheless spent with his family, while some of his colleagues spent it there.
keywords_en: dismissal of the public prosecutor general

sections.subtitle: Svi sveti, zrakoplov iznad Gibraltara i predsjednik koji se sam probija
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić opisuje kako se predsjednik Nawrocki iznad Gibraltara vratio u Poljsku
sections.content:
Datum akcije na Ustavnom sudu također je, prema gostu, svjesno izabran. Bili su to **Svi sveti**, kada se Varšava znatno isprazni jer velik dio stanovnika potječe iz manjih gradova i odlazi na grobove obitelji. Predsjednik je bio na putu u državni posjet Senegalu, a ni predsjednika Ustavnog suda Święczkowskog nije bilo u gradu. Andrijanić to sažima riječima: **„apsolutno tempirano”**.

Nawrocki je vijest da je policija ušla u Ustavni sud i da je sutkinja Anna Korin Pietrowska, kako je ime zabilježeno u transkriptu, objavila suspenziju Święczkowskog i potpredsjednika dobio u zrakoplovu **iznad Gibraltara**. Okrenuo je zrakoplov i vratio se u Poljsku. Voditeljica primjećuje da to zvuči „kao na filmu”. Andrijanić prepričava kako su ljudi okupljeni pred sudom na radaru pratili gdje se nalazi predsjednički zrakoplov.

Gost spominje i nagađanja, o kojima se kasnije pisalo, da se zrakoplov pokušalo preusmjeriti iz Varšave prema Wrocławu ili Krakovu. Ne bi bio iznenađen da je to istina. Činjenica da se preusmjeravanje nije dogodilo po njemu pokazuje da postoje podjele unutar samih institucija, vjerojatno i unutar vojnih struktura koje reguliraju let.

Nakon slijetanja Nawrocki se u predsjedničkoj palači sastao s potpredsjednikom Ustavnog suda i predsjednikom Vrhovnog suda. Obojica su mu, kaže Andrijanić, rekla da je Tuskov postupak nezakonit. Predsjednik je zatim limuzinom sa zaštitarima otišao pred Ustavni sud i probio se kroz gomilu.

Andrijanić je bio ondje. Policajce opisuje kao **„mlade, jadne, uplašene”** ljude koji nisu znali zašto su ondje, jer je operacija bila tajno planirana i nisu dobili informacije o tome kamo idu. Pred vratima je predsjednika čekala sutkinja koja ga je, prema snimkama, pokušala zaustaviti držeći ruke na njemu. Gost to naziva **narušavanjem tjelesnog integriteta predsjednika**. Da se to dogodilo američkom ili nekom drugom europskom predsjedniku, kaže, zaštitari bi je oborili na pod.

Nawrockijevim zaštitarima kasnije se prigovaralo što su to dopustili. Andrijanić je uvjeren da im je predsjednik sam rekao: **„Pustite to meni, ja ću to srediti”**, te da je išao prvi. Tumačenja da je riječ o napadu na sutkinju naziva glupostima i dijelom strategije da se Nawrockog prikaže kao „primitivnog huligana koji je postao predsjednik”.
sections.subtitle_en: All Saints' Day, an Airplane Over Gibraltar, and a President Breaking Through Alone
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić describes how President Nawrocki returned to Poland over Gibraltar
sections.content_en:
The date of the action at the Constitutional Court was also, according to the guest, deliberately chosen. It was **All Saints' Day**, when Warsaw empties out considerably because a large portion of the residents originate from smaller towns and go to family graves. The president was on his way for a state visit to Senegal, and Constitutional Court President Święczkowski was not in town either. Andrijanić summarizes this in the words: **“absolutely timed”**.

Nawrocki received the news that police had entered the Constitutional Court and that judge Anna Korin Pietrowska, as the name is recorded in the transcript, had announced the suspension of Święczkowski and the vice president while on the plane **over Gibraltar**. He turned the plane around and returned to Poland. The host remarks that it sounds “like in a movie”. Andrijanić recounts how people gathered in front of the court were tracking where the presidential aircraft was on radar.

The guest also mentions speculations, written about later, that there was an attempt to divert the plane from Warsaw toward Wrocław or Kraków. He would not be surprised if that were true. The fact that the diversion did not happen, according to him, shows that there are divisions within the institutions themselves, probably also within the military structures that regulate the flight.

After landing, Nawrocki met at the presidential palace with the vice president of the Constitutional Court and the president of the Supreme Court. Both, Andrijanić says, told him that Tusk's action was illegal. The president then went by limousine with security guards in front of the Constitutional Court and broke through the crowd.

Andrijanić was there. He describes the police officers as **“young, pathetic, scared”** people who did not know why they were there, because the operation had been secretly planned and they were not given information about where they were going. In front of the door, the president was awaited by the judge who, according to recordings, tried to stop him by putting her hands on him. The guest calls this **a violation of the bodily integrity of the president**. Had that happened to an American or some other European president, he says, security guards would have knocked her to the ground.

Nawrocki's security guards were later criticized for allowing that. Andrijanić is convinced that the president himself told them: **“Leave that to me, I will handle it”**, and that he went first. He calls interpretations that it was an assault on the judge nonsense and part of a strategy to portray Nawrocki as a “primitive hooligan who became president”.

sections.subtitle: Lažna vijest o njemačkoj policiji i strah od povratka prošlosti
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori kako policijski kordoni Poljake podsjećaju na komunističku represiju
sections.content:
Voditeljica navodi da je na mreži X te večeri kružilo mnogo informacija i snimki, među njima i tvrdnje o **njemačkoj policiji** u Varšavi. Andrijanić to odlučno demantira: „To nije istina.” Uz osmijeh dodaje da „čak i Tusk ima neke granice”.

Na pitanje kakva je bila atmosfera i shvaćaju li Poljaci moguće posljedice, odgovara da ih shvaćaju. U Poljskoj se raspravlja hoće li ovaj događaj naštetiti Tusku. Ojačati ga sigurno neće, ali može mu donijeti neku vrstu statusa quo.

Gost realno priznaje da je **rasprava o Ustavnom sudu za većinu ljudi apstraktna**. Usporedbe radi spominje Hrvatsku, gdje je, kako kaže, ono što je Milanović radio s Ustavom bilo „klasično antiustavno, antidemokratsko ponašanje”, a prošlo je praktički ispod radara.

Tuskov problem, međutim, leži drugdje. Policija u državnoj instituciji, policijski kordoni, kolone policijskih vozila koje stižu u Varšavu i mladi uplašeni policajci prizori su koje su Poljaci, kaže Andrijanić, već previše puta proživjeli u svojoj povijesti, i toga im je dosta. Liberalni komentator u Velikoj Britaniji može to protumačiti kao vraćanje vladavine prava. Čovjek koji je iskusio komunističku represiju u tome vidi **povratak na stare priče**. Gost zaključuje da se Tusk ovaj put ipak malo preračunao.
sections.subtitle_en: Fake News About German Police and the Fear of the Past Returning
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about how police cordons remind Poles of communist repression
sections.content_en:
The host states that on the X network that evening many pieces of information and recordings circulated, among them claims about **German police** in Warsaw. Andrijanić decisively denies this: “That is not true.” With a smile he adds that “even Tusk has some limits”.

To the question of what the atmosphere was like and whether Poles understand the possible consequences, he answers that they understand them. In Poland there is a debate over whether this event will harm Tusk. It certainly will not strengthen him, but it can bring him some kind of status quo.

The guest realistically admits that **the debate about the Constitutional Court is abstract for most people**. For the sake of comparison, he mentions Croatia, where, as he says, what Milanović did with the Constitution was “classic anti-constitutional, anti-democratic behavior”, and passed practically under the radar.

Tusk's problem, however, lies elsewhere. Police in a state institution, police cordons, columns of police vehicles arriving in Warsaw, and young frightened police officers are scenes that Poles, says Andrijanić, have experienced too many times in their history, and they have had enough of it. A liberal commentator in Great Britain might interpret this as restoring the rule of law. A person who experienced communist repression sees in it **a return to old stories**. The guest concludes that Tusk miscalculated a bit this time after all.

sections.subtitle: Meta broj jedan: središnja banka, 673 tone zlata i euro
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić govori o zlatnim rezervama Poljske središnje banke
sections.content:
Voditeljica se vraća na kulturni rat i pita što konkretno „globalisti” žele od Poljske. Navodi sadržaje s društvenih mreža o ukidanju zlota, predaji zlata europskoj banci, otvaranju granica i LGBTQ politikama. Andrijanić odgovara konkretnim primjerom **Poljske središnje banke**.

Njezin je guverner **Adam Głapiński**, kojega gost opisuje kao vrlo cijenjenog ekonomista bliskog krugovima PiS-a. Prema njegovim saznanjima nikada nije bio član stranke, ali je bio u Solidarnosti. Głapiński je nagomilao oko **673 tone zlata**, što je, ističe Andrijanić, više nego što ima Europska središnja banka. U vrijeme pandemije povukao je poteze koji su ublažili posljedice za male i srednje poduzetnike i pomogao je u kontroli inflacije.

Andrijanić tu vidi i ideološki spor. Głapiński zagovara određeni intervencionizam, odnosno stav da središnja banka smije pomoći državi kada je to potrebno. Upravo zbog toga postoji inicijativa da ga se izvede pred **Državni sud** jer je navodno prekoračio ovlasti. Gost tvrdi da ga se time zapravo želi kazniti zato što je „de facto spasio Poljsku”. Zasad to ne mogu provesti jer mu mandat još traje, ali je Tusk, kaže, „već bacio oko na to zlato”.

Pozadina je, prema Andrijaniću, ogroman proračunski deficit koji usporava gospodarstvo, uz zdravstveni sustav u raspadu, u kojem se **zatvaraju bolnice i rodilišta**. Zlatom bi se moglo pokrpati deficit. Druga mogućnost je da zlato završi u Frankfurtu kad Poljska uvede euro, što Tusk, kaže gost, ni ne skriva kao jedan od glavnih ciljeva. Głapiński i konzervativni tabor oštri su protivnici eura. Andrijanić zaključuje da bi preuzimanje središnje banke bilo znatno lakše kada bi Tusk kontrolirao i Ustavni sud.
sections.subtitle_en: Target Number One: The Central Bank, 673 Tons of Gold, and the Euro
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić speaks about the gold reserves of the Polish Central Bank
sections.content_en:
The host returns to the culture war and asks what specifically the “globalists” want from Poland. She mentions content from social networks about abolishing the zloty, surrendering gold to the European bank, opening borders, and LGBTQ policies. Andrijanić responds with the concrete example of the **National Bank of Poland**.

Its governor is **Adam Glapiński**, whom the guest describes as a highly respected economist close to PiS circles. According to his information, he was never a member of the party, but he was in Solidarity. Glapiński accumulated about **673 tons of gold**, which is, Andrijanić points out, more than the European Central Bank holds. During the pandemic, he made moves that softened the consequences for small and medium-sized entrepreneurs and helped in controlling inflation.

Andrijanić also sees an ideological dispute here. Glapiński advocates a certain interventionism, that is, the stance that the central bank is permitted to assist the state when necessary. Precisely because of that, there is an initiative to bring him before the **State Tribunal** because he allegedly exceeded his powers. The guest claims that they actually want to punish him for “de facto saving Poland”. For now they cannot carry it out because his mandate is still running, but Tusk, he says, has “already set his sights on that gold”.

The background, according to Andrijanić, is a huge budget deficit that is slowing down the economy, along with a healthcare system in collapse, in which **hospitals and maternity wards are closing**. With the gold, the deficit could be patched. The other possibility is that the gold ends up in Frankfurt when Poland introduces the euro, which Tusk, says the guest, does not even hide as one of his main goals. Glapiński and the conservative camp are fierce opponents of the euro. Andrijanić concludes that taking over the central bank would be significantly easier if Tusk also controlled the Constitutional Court.

sections.subtitle: Eugenički pobačaj i sabotirani prometni čvor
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o najavi maršala Sejma da će zatražiti legalizaciju eugeničkog pobačaja
sections.content:
Drugi front ideološkog rata, prema Andrijaniću, jest pitanje nacionalne tradicije i vjernosti katoličkim idealima, a posebno **pobačaja**. Ustavni sud je 2020. zabranio eugenički pobačaj, odnosno pobačaj u slučaju bolesti djeteta. Gost navodi da se ta odredba u većini slučajeva koristila za pobačaje djece s Downovim sindromom. Zabrana je tada izazvala prosvjede.

Kao svjež primjer navodi događaj od dana prije snimanja. Iako novi ustavni sustav još nije ni počeo funkcionirati, predsjednik Sejma **Włodzimierz Czarzasty** objavio je da će kao maršal podnijeti zahtjev za opoziv te odluke, kako bi se eugenički pobačaj ponovno legalizirao. Voditeljica to naziva primjerom ideološkog rata, a gost se slaže i dodaje da je taj rat povezan i s pitanjem suverenosti.

U tom kontekstu Andrijanić ponovno spominje **CPK**, središnji prometni čvor. Opisuje ga kao savršen primjer projekta koji je trebao dodatno pozicionirati Poljsku na gospodarskoj karti srednje Europe, a sabotiran je, kako tvrdi, zato što je bio **konkurentan Njemačkoj**. Rat se, zaključuje, vodi u različitim dimenzijama.
sections.subtitle_en: Eugenic Abortion and the Sabotaged Transport Hub
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the announcement by the Marshal of the Sejm that he will seek the legalization of eugenic abortion
sections.content_en:
The second front of the ideological war, according to Andrijanić, is the question of national tradition and loyalty to Catholic ideals, and especially **abortion**. In 2020, the Constitutional Court banned eugenic abortion, namely abortion in cases of fetal impairment. The guest states that this provision was used in most cases for abortions of children with Down syndrome. The ban sparked protests at the time.

As a fresh example, he cites an event from the day before the recording. Although the new constitutional system has not even begun to function yet, Sejm Marshal **Włodzimierz Czarzasty** announced that as marshal he would submit a request to repeal that decision, so that eugenic abortion would be legalized again. The host calls this an example of ideological war, and the guest agrees and adds that this war is also connected to the question of sovereignty.

In that context, Andrijanić again mentions the **CPK**, the central transport hub. He describes it as a perfect example of a project that was supposed to further position Poland on the economic map of Central Europe, and was sabotaged, as he claims, because it was **competitive with Germany**. The war, he concludes, is being waged in different dimensions.

sections.subtitle: Tusk iz hrvatske perspektive: „provincijalni kompleks” i progresivni resori
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić govori o Tuskovoj autobiografiji i njegovu pogledu na rat u Jugoslaviji
sections.content:
Govoreći o istospolnim brakovima, koje Poljska ne priznaje, Andrijanić se osvrće na Tuskov ugled u Hrvatskoj. Ima dojam da Tusk u dijelu hrvatskih konzervativnih krugova, posebno oko HDZ-a, uživa dobru reputaciju. To pripisuje **„provincijalnom kompleksu”**, prema kojemu se nekoga voli zato što je kao Poljak napravio karijeru u Bruxellesu pa se pretpostavlja da brani i naše interese. Gost je izravan: Tusk ne brani ničije interese osim vlastitih, a prema Hrvatskoj je potpuno indiferentan i ne razumije hrvatsku državotvornost.

Kao dokaz navodi Tuskovu autobiografsku knjigu pod naslovom, kako je zabilježeno u transkriptu, *Iskreno*. Gost je smatra svime samo ne iskrenom. U njoj Tusk, prema Andrijanićevu prepričavanju, rat u Jugoslaviji prikazuje kao rezultat nacionalističkog ludila Hrvata i Srba koji se zapravo vole i zajedno piju rakiju. Gost to naziva glupostima.

Iako se Tusk predstavljao kao „umiren narodnjak”, najvažnije je resore, kaže Andrijanić, prepustio progresivnoj ljevici. Ministarstvo obrazovanja vodi Barbara Novacka, koju opisuje kao žestoku feministkinju i „praktički marksisticu”. Postojalo je i ministarstvo ravnopravnosti spolova, koje je vodila Kataržina Kotula, a koje je kasnije ukinuto.

Najapsurdnijim smatra to što je **Włodzimierz Czarzasty**, šef Nove ljevice, postao maršal Sejma s, kako tvrdi, dvadesetak tisuća osvojenih glasova. Na tu je funkciju došao zahvaljujući koalicijskom sporazumu i sada, kaže gost, „terorizira apsolutno sve oko sebe”. Glavna mu je zadaća, smatra Andrijanić, voditi rat s Nawrockim. Predsjednik ima pravo slati zakonske inicijative u Sejm, a maršal ih upućuje u raspravu. Czarzasty je, prema gostu, **blokirao apsolutno sve Nawrockijeve prijedloge**.

Napadi su usmjereni i na Crkvu. Ljevica, navodi Andrijanić, želi ukinuti fond kojim se, u okviru konkordata sa Svetom Stolicom, Crkvi nadoknađuje imovina koju su komunisti zaplijenili nakon Drugog svjetskog rata. Hoće li se to dogoditi, zasad je otvoreno. Gost zaključuje da Tusk kao cinični političar koristi postkomunističke strukture za učvršćivanje vlastite pozicije i „pušta komuniste da divljaju”.
sections.subtitle_en: Tusk from the Croatian Perspective: “Provincial Complex” and Progressive Portfolios
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić speaks about Tusk's autobiography and his view of the war in Yugoslavia
sections.content_en:
Speaking about same-sex marriages, which Poland does not recognize, Andrijanić reflects on Tusk's reputation in Croatia. He has the impression that Tusk enjoys a good reputation in part of Croatian conservative circles, especially around the HDZ. He attributes this to a **“provincial complex”**, according to which someone is liked because as a Pole he made a career in Brussels, so it is assumed that he defends our interests as well. The guest is direct: Tusk defends nobody's interests except his own, and toward Croatia he is completely indifferent and does not understand Croatian statehood.

As proof, he cites Tusk's autobiographical book titled, as recorded in the transcript, *Honestly*. The guest considers it anything but honest. In it Tusk, according to Andrijanić's recounting, portrays the war in Yugoslavia as the result of nationalist madness of Croats and Serbs who actually love each other and drink rakija together. The guest calls this nonsense.

Although Tusk presented himself as a “moderate popular party member”, he left the most important portfolios, says Andrijanić, to the progressive left. The Ministry of Education is headed by Barbara Nowacka, whom he describes as a fierce feminist and “practically a Marxist”. There was also a ministry for gender equality, headed by Katarzyna Kotula, which was later abolished.

He considers most absurd that **Włodzimierz Czarzasty**, head of the New Left, became Marshal of the Sejm with, as he claims, some twenty thousand votes won. He came to that position thanks to a coalition agreement and now, says the guest, “terrorizes absolutely everyone around him”. His main task, Andrijanić considers, is to wage war against Nawrocki. The president has the right to send legislative initiatives to the Sejm, and the marshal refers them to debate. Czarzasty, according to the guest, **blocked absolutely all of Nawrocki's proposals**.

Attacks are also directed at the Church. The left, Andrijanić states, wants to abolish the fund by which, within the framework of the concordat with the Holy See, the Church is compensated for property that the communists confiscated after the Second World War. Whether that will happen is open for now. The guest concludes that Tusk, as a cynical politician, uses post-communist structures to consolidate his own position and “lets the communists run amok”.

sections.subtitle: Zašto Poljska nije provela lustraciju: Wałęsa, „debela crta” i noćna smjena
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić objašnjava pojam „debele crte” Tadeusza Mazowieckog
sections.content:
Voditeljica traži kratak odgovor na pitanje zašto Poljska nije provela lustraciju. Andrijanić odgovara u nekoliko koraka.

**Prvo, slučaj Wałęsa.** Gost je nedavno pisao o tome da je definitivno potvrđeno da je Lech Wałęsa u prvoj polovici sedamdesetih bio suradnik komunističkih službi. To više nije predmet spora. Danas se raspravlja o tome što je službama govorio, je li od njih dobivao novac i kako je to utjecalo na njegovo kasnije djelovanje kao vođe Solidarnosti i prvog demokratski izabranog predsjednika.

**Drugo, okrugli stol i „debela crta”.** Prvi premijer nakon prvih izbora, Tadeusz Mazowiecki, najavio je da će se povući „debela crta” prema prošlosti, u smislu: što je bilo, bilo je. To je, prema gostu, izazvalo nezadovoljstvo dijela Solidarnosti.

**Treće, noćna smjena.** Oko 1992. vladu je vodio Jan Olszewski, odvjetnik koji je u komunističkim procesima branio aktiviste Solidarnosti. Andrijanić ga opisuje kao žestokog idealista koji se možda izgubio u politici jer je bio previše idealističan. Njegova je vlada počela istraživati dosjee i izradila popis bivših suradnika komunističkih službi, na kojemu su se našli i ljudi s političkim funkcijama u novoj državi. Prema gostovu sjećanju, u lipnju 1992. Wałęsa je kao predsjednik preko noći inicirao glasovanje o povjerenju i Olszewskijeva je vlada pala. Taj događaj pamti se kao **„noćna smjena”**, a Andrijanić ga smatra indikativnim za to kako je lustracija zaustavljena.

**Četvrto, povratak postkomunista.** Već 1993. na vlast su se vratili postkomunisti, zbog nezadovoljstva elitama Solidarnosti koje su se međusobno svađale, među ostalim i oko lustracije. Voditeljica to sažima riječima da je trebalo „čistiti sami sebe”.

Andrijanić ipak dodaje da Poljska, za razliku od Hrvatske, lustraciju na određeni način i dalje provodi, i to kroz **Institut nacionalnog sjećanja (IPN)**, osnovan krajem devedesetih. Gost smatra pravim čudom što je ta institucija preživjela. Upravo su njezini stručnjaci dokazali Wałęsinu suradnju. Pritom naglašava da nema dokaza o suradnji u vrijeme same Solidarnosti. Otvoreno ostaje pitanje koliko su ga službe mogle ucjenjivati onime što su imale u dosjeu. Neki tvrde da je Wałęsa spriječio novi štrajk nakon Gdanjska koji je mogao promijeniti situaciju. Ta se previranja, zaključuje gost, nastavljaju i danas.
sections.subtitle_en: Why Poland Did Not Carry Out Lustration: Wałęsa, the “Thick Line”, and the Night Shift
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić explains Tadeusz Mazowiecki's concept of the “thick line”
sections.content_en:
The host asks for a short answer to the question of why Poland did not carry out lustration. Andrijanić replies in several steps.

**First, the Wałęsa case.** The guest recently wrote about it being definitively confirmed that Lech Wałęsa in the first half of the seventies was a collaborator with the communist secret services. That is no longer a matter of dispute. Today what is debated is what he told the services, whether he received money from them, and how that influenced his later activity as leader of Solidarity and the first democratically elected president.

**Second, the round table and the “thick line”.** The first prime minister after the first elections, Tadeusz Mazowiecki, announced that a “thick line” would be drawn with respect to the past, in the sense: what happened, happened. That, according to the guest, caused dissatisfaction among part of Solidarity.

**Third, the night shift.** Around 1992, the government was led by Jan Olszewski, a lawyer who in communist trials had defended Solidarity activists. Andrijanić describes him as a fierce idealist who perhaps got lost in politics because he was overly idealistic. His government began investigating dossiers and drew up a list of former collaborators with the communist services, on which people with political functions in the new state were also found. According to the guest's recollection, in June 1992 Wałęsa, as president, overnight initiated a vote of confidence and Olszewski's government fell. That event is remembered as the **“night shift”**, and Andrijanić considers it indicative of how lustration was stopped.

**Fourth, the return of the post-communists.** As early as 1993, post-communists returned to power due to dissatisfaction with the elites of Solidarity, who quarreled among themselves, among other things over lustration. The host summarizes this with the words that it was necessary to “cleanse oneself”.

Andrijanić nevertheless adds that Poland, unlike Croatia, still carries out lustration in a certain way, specifically through the **Institute of National Remembrance (IPN)**, founded in the late nineties. The guest considers it a real miracle that this institution survived. It was its experts who proved Wałęsa's collaboration. In doing so, he emphasizes that there is no evidence of collaboration during the time of Solidarity itself. The question remains open as to how much the services could blackmail him with what they had in his dossier. Some claim that Wałęsa prevented a new strike after Gdańsk that could have changed the situation. Those upheavals, the guest concludes, continue today.

sections.subtitle: Rusija kao prijetnja: nepovjerenje utemeljeno u povijesti, a ne „rusofobija”
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić odgovara da je Rusija najveća sigurnosna prijetnja Poljskoj i Europi
sections.content:
Voditeljica, koja se gostu obraća s „Gorane”, prelazi na geopolitiku i pita je li Rusija danas najveća sigurnosna prijetnja Poljskoj. Andrijanić odgovara potvrdno: Rusija je **najveća sigurnosna prijetnja ne samo Poljskoj, nego cijeloj Europi**.

Kaže da ga posebno živcira priča o poljskoj „rusofobiji”. Poljski stav prema Rusima temelji se na povijesnom iskustvu: Poljaci su s Rusima uvijek ratovali, a Rusi su prema njima bili iznimno brutalni. Kao primjer o kojemu se malo govori navodi kraj 18. stoljeća, kada su generali Katarine Druge kod Varšave, u dijelu grada s druge strane Visle, **ubili oko trideset tisuća civila**, bez rata. Gost dodaje da je pokojni papa Franjo Katarinu Drugu kasnije opisao kao veliku ličnost ruske državotvornosti.

Rusofobija bi, objašnjava Andrijanić, bila nešto iracionalno, odnosno neutemeljena netrpeljivost. Poljska skepsa prema Rusiji utemeljena je. U poljskoj političkoj misli nema ozbiljne snage koja nije bila barem skeptična prema ruskom imperijalizmu. Bilo je pojedinaca koji su budućnost vidjeli u suradnji s Rusijom, ali to nikada nije bila ozbiljna struja.
sections.subtitle_en: Russia as a Threat: Distrust Grounded in History, Not “Russophobia”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić answers that Russia is the greatest security threat to Poland and Europe
sections.content_en:
The host, who addresses the guest as “Goran”, moves to geopolitics and asks whether Russia is today the greatest security threat to Poland. Andrijanić answers affirmatively: Russia is **the greatest security threat not only to Poland, but to all of Europe**.

He says that talk about Polish “Russophobia” especially annoys him. The Polish attitude toward Russians is based on historical experience: Poles always fought wars with Russians, and Russians were exceptionally brutal toward them. As an example about which little is said, he cites the late 18th century, when generals of Catherine the Great near Warsaw, in the part of the city on the other side of the Vistula, **killed about thirty thousand civilians**, without a war. The guest adds that the late Pope Francis later described Catherine the Great as a great figure of Russian statehood.

Russophobia, Andrijanić explains, would be something irrational, that is, unfounded hostility. Polish skepticism toward Russia is well-founded. In Polish political thought there is no serious force that was not at least skeptical of Russian imperialism. There were individuals who saw a future in cooperation with Russia, but that was never a serious current.

sections.subtitle: Tuskov reset s Moskvom i upozorenja braće Kaczyński
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira riječi Lecha Kaczyńskog iz Tbilisija
sections.content:
Andrijanić zatim iznosi tvrdnju za koju kaže da o njoj „ljudi nemaju pojma”: čovjek koji je u jednom trenutku forsirao savez s Rusijom bio je upravo **Donald Tusk**. Nakon pogibije Lecha Kaczyńskog u Smolensku 2010. počeo je, kako opisuje, poljsko-ruski reset usmjeravan iz Njemačke. Prema gostu, glavni izvršitelji bili su Tusk i ministar vanjskih poslova Radosław Sikorski, koji tu dužnost obnaša i danas. Razdoblje traje otprilike od 2010. do 2015., kada se Njemačka približavala Rusiji i kada je u igri bio Sjeverni tok.

Gost smatra točnom ocjenu koja se, kako kaže, često čuje u Poljskoj: rat u Ukrajini ima dva krivca, **Vladimira Putina i Angelu Merkel**. Merkel je, prema njemu, vodila politiku koja je ponovno ojačala Rusiju, izgradila njemačko gospodarstvo na jeftinim ruskim energentima i ruski stroj napunila novcem. U vrijeme reseta Putin je, kaže, često dolazio u Poljsku, energetska suradnja bila je intenzivna, a Gazprom je s poljskom državom sklopio vrlo unosne poslove.

Braća Kaczyński, nasuprot tome, uvijek su kritizirala ruski imperijalizam. Andrijanić podsjeća na rat u Gruziji, kada je Lech Kaczyński s nekoliko srednjoeuropskih čelnika otišao u Tbilisi i izrekao poznate riječi: **„Danas Gruzija, sutra Ukrajina, a prekosutra baltičke države ili možda čak moja domovina.”** Jarosław Kaczyński je nakon bratove smrti upozoravao da je ideja kako će poslovanje pacificirati Rusiju promašena. Zbog toga su ga, ističe gost, kritizirali upravo Tusk i Sikorski, koji danas sebe prikazuju kao proeuropske i prodemokratske, a njihove protivnike kao proruske.

Andrijanić ističe paradokse: Karol Nawrocki nalazi se na ruskoj tjeralici jer je rušio spomenike Crvenoj armiji. Bez vojne i diplomatske pomoći vlasti Jarosława Kaczyńskog, tvrdi gost, Kijeva u prvim danima agresije „ne bi bilo”, iako najveća zasluga pripada herojstvu Ukrajinaca. O Sikorskom pak tvrdi da je za vrijeme Majdana 2014. nagovarao Ukrajince da popuste proruskim snagama, a danas se predstavlja kao borac protiv ruskog imperijalizma. Voditeljica to opisuje kao „mentalnu vrtoglavicu”.
sections.subtitle_en: Tusk's Reset with Moscow and the Warnings of the Kaczyński Brothers
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes the words of Lech Kaczyński from Tbilisi
sections.content_en:
Andrijanić then presents a claim about which he says “people have no idea”: the man who at one point pushed for an alliance with Russia was none other than **Donald Tusk**. After the death of Lech Kaczyński in Smolensk in 2010, there began, as he describes, a Polish-Russian reset directed from Germany. According to the guest, the main executors were Tusk and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, who holds that office today as well. The period lasts approximately from 2010 to 2015, when Germany was drawing closer to Russia and when Nord Stream was in play.

The guest considers accurate the assessment that, as he says, is often heard in Poland: the war in Ukraine has two culprits, **Vladimir Putin and Angela Merkel**. Merkel, according to him, led a policy that made Russia strong again, built the German economy on cheap Russian energy resources, and filled the Russian machine with money. At the time of the reset, Putin, he says, often came to Poland, energy cooperation was intensive, and Gazprom concluded very lucrative deals with the Polish state.

The Kaczyński brothers, by contrast, always criticized Russian imperialism. Andrijanić recalls the war in Georgia, when Lech Kaczyński went to Tbilisi with several Central European leaders and uttered the famous words: **“Today Georgia, tomorrow Ukraine, and the day after tomorrow the Baltic states or perhaps even my homeland.”** After his brother's death, Jarosław Kaczyński warned that the idea that business would pacify Russia was misguided. Because of this, the guest points out, he was criticized precisely by Tusk and Sikorski, who today portray themselves as pro-European and pro-democratic, and their opponents as pro-Russian.

Andrijanić highlights paradoxes: Karol Nawrocki is on the Russian wanted list because he tore down monuments to the Red Army. Without the military and diplomatic assistance of the government of Jarosław Kaczyński, the guest claims, Kyiv in the first days of aggression “would not exist”, although the greatest credit belongs to the heroism of the Ukrainians. Concerning Sikorski, he claims that during the Maidan in 2014 he urged Ukrainians to yield to pro-Russian forces, while today he presents himself as a fighter against Russian imperialism. The host describes this as “mental vertigo”.

sections.subtitle: Šutnja hrvatskih konzervativaca i Janšina hrabrost
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić kritizira šutnju hrvatskih suverenističkih stranaka
sections.content:
Andrijanić priznaje da ponekad osjeća zasićenje. Kada pogleda **letargiju i „političku žabokrečevinu” u Hrvatskoj**, kaže da je Bogu zahvalan što se preselio. Voditeljica ga potiče da to pojasni.

Gost smatra nevjerojatnim da četvrti dan traje, kako ga naziva, državni udar, a da se **nijedna hrvatska konzervativna i suverenistička stranka nije oglasila**. Na pitanje zašto, kaže da ne zna i da ne bi to nazvao kukavičlukom. Šutnju Domovinskog pokreta razumije jer je u koaliciji s HDZ-om, koji je u istoj europskoj stranačkoj obitelji kao i Tuskova stranka. Dodaje i da je Domovinski pokret po njegovu mišljenju „već gotova priča”. Ne razumije, međutim, zašto šuti Most, koji je u ECR-u kao i PiS i čiji se čelnici slikaju na konferencijama lidera PiS-a, kao ni zašto šuti Domino.

Upozorava da je situacija u Poljskoj **univerzalna i da se sutra može dogoditi u Hrvatskoj**. Riječ je, prema njemu, o teroru globalističke liberalne demokracije nad suverenističkim snagama. U komentaru na portalu Misao.hr napisao je da PiS u vrijeme svoje vlasti nije napravio ni deset posto, nego ni 0,1 posto onoga što sada radi Tusk, a da bi, kako karikira, „tenkovi NATO-a bili na granici”. Danas Tusk, „naš čovjek, Europljanin, veliki demokrat”, postupa poput diktatora u banana-državi, i nitko ništa ne poduzima. Hrvatskim suverenistima poručuje da, ako sada šute, sutra ne očekuju ničiju pomoć. Takvu šutnju naziva kukavičlukom i nedostatkom šire slike.

Kao suprotan primjer navodi **Janeza Janšu**, koji je u istoj Europskoj pučkoj stranci kao i Tusk, a ipak je javno pitao je li to Europska unija u koju smo ulazili ako se policija šalje na Ustavni sud. Voditeljica dodaje da je Janša objavu na mreži X završio riječima: **„Nastala je Europska unija koja se mora spašavati sama od sebe.”** Na pitanje je li Janša hrabriji od hrvatskih političara, Andrijanić odgovara: „Apsolutno.” Prema razgovorima sa slovenskim poznanicima, bio je to riskantan korak koji će mu zakomplicirati odnose s Nijemcima u EPP-u. Kada se zamjeraš Nijemcima, kaže gost, zamjeraš se i Bruxellesu.

Voditeljica pita hoće li se i on zamjeriti. Andrijanić prepričava kako mu je kolega dan ranije rekao da je situacija neizvjesna. Ideju građanskog rata ipak smatra pretjeranom. S humorom zaključuje da se svima kojima se trebao zamjeriti, i u Hrvatskoj i u Poljskoj, već odavno zamjerio.
sections.subtitle_en: The Silence of Croatian Conservatives and Janša's Courage
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić criticizes the silence of Croatian sovereignist parties
sections.content_en:
Andrijanić admits that he sometimes feels burnout. When he looks at the **lethargy and „political backwater” in Croatia**, he says he is grateful to God that he moved. The host encourages him to clarify this.

The guest considers it incredible that for four days, what he calls a coup d'état has been going on, without **a single Croatian conservative and sovereignist party speaking out**. Asked why, he says he does not know and that he would not call it cowardice. He understands the silence of the Homeland Movement because it is in a coalition with HDZ, which is in the same European party family as Tusk's party. He also adds that the Homeland Movement is, in his opinion, „already a finished story”. He does not understand, however, why Most is silent, which is in the ECR just like PiS and whose leaders take photos at conferences of PiS leaders, nor why Domino is silent.

He warns that the situation in Poland is **universal and could happen tomorrow in Croatia**. It is, according to him, a terror of globalist liberal democracy over sovereignist forces. In a commentary on the portal Misao.hr, he wrote that PiS during its time in power did not do even ten percent, indeed not even 0.1 percent of what Tusk is doing now, and that, as he caricatures, „NATO tanks would be on the border”. Today Tusk, „our man, a European, a great democrat”, acts like a dictator in a banana republic, and no one is doing anything. He tells Croatian sovereignists that if they remain silent now, they should not expect anyone's help tomorrow. He calls such silence cowardice and a lack of the broader picture.

As a contrary example, he cites **Janez Janša**, who is in the same European People's Party as Tusk, and yet publicly asked whether this is the European Union we entered if the police are sent to the Constitutional Court. The host adds that Janša ended his post on the X network with the words: **„A European Union has emerged that must save itself from itself.”** Asked whether Janša is braver than Croatian politicians, Andrijanić replies: „Absolutely.” According to conversations with Slovenian acquaintances, it was a risky step that will complicate his relations with the Germans in the EPP. When you cross the Germans, the guest says, you also cross Brussels.

The host asks whether he too will cross them. Andrijanić recounts how a colleague told him the day before that the situation was uncertain. However, he considers the idea of a civil war exaggerated. With humor, he concludes that he has long since crossed everyone he needed to cross, both in Croatia and in Poland.

sections.subtitle: Rat s Rusijom, naoružavanje i pitanje zaštitnika
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje Tuskovo oslanjanje na EU i Nawrockijevo oslanjanje na SAD
sections.content:
Na pitanje koliko je realan sukob Poljske i Rusije, Andrijanić odgovara da ga **kratkoročno smatra nerealnim**. Rusija za to ima vojne kapacitete, ali joj se dalja eskalacija trenutačno ne isplati. Dugoročno je oprezniji: ako Putin ostane na vlasti, nema sumnje da će se jednom pojaviti trenutak u kojem će joj se to isplatiti.

Zato smatra da je za svaku razumnu državu ključno da se **naoružava što je jače moguće**. Hrvati, kaže, mogu Bogu zahvaliti što je ministar obrane **Anušić**, kojega opisuje kao svjesnog geopolitičkih opasnosti. Kao razlog navodi susjednu Srbiju, koju vidi kao nestabilnu državu koja se „radikalno naoružala”. Ideju da bi Srbija u sljedećih dvadesetak do trideset godina mogla dosegnuti demokratske standarde naziva znanstvenom fantastikom. Po njegovoj procjeni Srbija će uvijek biti pijun u rukama Rusije, bez obzira na igru koju je Vučić igrao.

Oštro kritizira i dijelove hrvatske javnosti, pa i Crkve, kada biskupi govore o strahu od rata i štetnosti naoružanja. To smatra neodgovornim u trenutku kada se **mijenja cijeli geopolitički kontekst**. Kaže da nije veliki geopolitički stručnjak, ali da to vidi zdravim razumom: „Tko to ne vidi, ne vidi ništa.”

Gost potom opisuje razliku između dvojice poljskih čelnika u pitanju oslonca:

- **Tusk** se oslanja na Europsku uniju, koja, prema Andrijaniću, nema vojnih kapaciteta ni za što. Kao primjer navodi Grenland, kamo je poslano nekoliko njemačkih vojnika koji su se, kako se šali, nakon tjedan dana zbog vremena vratili kući, „iako u Njemačkoj isto nije baš puno ljepše vrijeme”.
- **Nawrocki** se oslanja na Ameriku, bez obzira na to tko je u Washingtonu.

Za Hrvatsku zaključuje da kao manji narod mora odabrati svog zaštitnika, ali se prije toga mora **naoružavati sama za sebe**. Iako, kako kaže, nema mnogo dobrih riječi za vlast HDZ-a, Anušića smatra „praktički jedinom svijetlom točkom” u toj priči.
sections.subtitle_en: War with Russia, Armament, and the Question of a Protector
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares Tusk's reliance on the EU and Nawrocki's reliance on the USA
sections.content_en:
Asked how realistic a conflict between Poland and Russia is, Andrijanić replies that **in the short term, he considers it unrealistic**. Russia has the military capacity for it, but further escalation is currently not worth it for them. In the long term, he is more cautious: if Putin remains in power, there is no doubt that a moment will eventually come when it will be worth it for them.

That is why he considers it crucial for every reasonable state to **arm itself as strongly as possible**. Croats, he says, can thank God that the defense minister is **Anušić**, whom he describes as aware of geopolitical dangers. As a reason, he cites neighboring Serbia, which he sees as an unstable state that has „radically armed itself”. The idea that Serbia could reach democratic standards in the next twenty to thirty years he calls science fiction. In his assessment, Serbia will always be a pawn in the hands of Russia, regardless of the game Vučić played.

He also sharply criticizes parts of the Croatian public, and even of the Church, when bishops speak about the fear of war and the harmfulness of armament. He considers this irresponsible at a moment when the **entire geopolitical context is changing**. He says he is not a great geopolitical expert, but that he sees this with common sense: „Whoever does not see this, sees nothing.”

The guest then describes the difference between the two Polish leaders regarding their reliance:

- **Tusk** relies on the European Union, which, according to Andrijanić, has no military capacity for anything. As an example, he mentions Greenland, where several German soldiers were sent who, as he jokes, returned home after a week due to the weather, „even though the weather in Germany isn't really that much nicer either”.
- **Nawrocki** relies on America, regardless of who is in Washington.

For Croatia, he concludes that as a smaller nation it must choose its protector, but before that, it must **arm itself on its own**. Although, as he says, he does not have many good words for the HDZ government, he considers Anušić „practically the only bright spot” in that story.

sections.subtitle: Pouke za Hrvatsku: srednjoeuropski identitet, Tri mora i nada u pravog državnika
sections.screenshot_description: Andrijanić govori o inicijativi Tri mora kao hrvatskoj perspektivi
sections.content:
Na završno pitanje što bi Hrvatska trebala naučiti iz poljskog primjera, Andrijanić odgovara da prije svega treba **voditi računa o svom identitetu, posebno o srednjoeuropskom**. Državnu politiku treba graditi na temeljima koji Hrvatskoj donose sigurnost, zaštitu i prosperitet, a ne na osobnim interesima ili „sinekurama u Bruxellesu”.

Kao konkretan okvir navodi **inicijativu Tri mora**, koja, nažalost, još nije do kraja ostvarena. U njoj on, kao i, kako kaže, svaki razuman sugovornik u Hrvatskoj, vidi stvarnu perspektivu. Crta između Baltika i Jadrana za njega je „naša priča” u identitetskom, kulturnom, političkom i sigurnosnom smislu. Napominje i da je projekt pod izravnim pokroviteljstvom Sjedinjenih Država. Voditeljica poruku sažima riječima „ostati svoji što više”, a gost dodaje: biti istinski posvećen dobru naroda.

Takvu posvećenost vidi kod poljskih političara. O Nawrockom se može govoriti što god tko hoće, kaže, ali se vidi da mu je interes naroda na srcu, a isto vrijedi i za Kaczyńskog. Na voditeljičino pitanje vidi li takvog političara u Hrvatskoj, nakon kratke stanke odgovara kratko: **„Ne.”** Voditeljica primjećuje da nije prvi sugovornik koji joj je tako odgovorio i da se time otvara osjećaj beznađa, jer je Hrvatska ipak manja zemlja od Poljske.

Andrijanić ipak završava s nadom. Prepričava razgovor svoje supruge s jednom Hrvaticom, koja je rekla da Bog u presudnim trenucima uvijek šalje prave državnike narodima koji su mu vjerni. Hrvati su imali **Tuđmana** kad su ga trebali, a Poljaci sada imaju Nawrockog. Gost vjeruje da bi se uskoro i u Hrvatskoj mogao pojaviti čovjek koji će biti „emanacija onoga najboljega u hrvatskom nacionalnom biću”. Voditeljica dodaje da se za njega treba moliti, s čime se gost slaže.

Na kraju voditeljica zahvaljuje gostu. Razgovor je bio planiran za četrdeset i pet minuta, a trajao je više od sat vremena. Andrijanić se ispričava ako je „malo prebrljavao”. Kaže da se u njemu mnogo toga nakupilo, a kada ima priliku govoriti na hrvatskom, teško ga je zaustaviti. Oboje izražavaju nadu da im ovo nije bio posljednji razgovor.
sections.subtitle_en: Lessons for Croatia: Central European Identity, the Three Seas, and Hope in a True Statesman
sections.screenshot_description_en: Andrijanić speaks about the Three Seas Initiative as a Croatian perspective
sections.content_en:
To the final question of what Croatia should learn from the Polish example, Andrijanić replies that first of all it must **take care of its identity, especially Central European**. State policy should be built on foundations that bring security, protection, and prosperity to Croatia, not on personal interests or „sinecures in Brussels”.

As a concrete framework, he cites the **Three Seas Initiative**, which, unfortunately, has not yet been fully realized. In it, he, like, as he says, every reasonable interlocutor in Croatia, sees a real perspective. The line between the Baltic and the Adriatic is for him „our story” in an identity, cultural, political, and security sense. He also notes that the project is under the direct patronage of the United States. The host summarizes the message with the words „remain ourselves as much as possible”, and the guest adds: be truly dedicated to the good of the people.

He sees such dedication among Polish politicians. One can say whatever one wants about Nawrocki, he says, but one can see that he has the people's interest at heart, and the same goes for Kaczyński. To the host's question whether he sees such a politician in Croatia, after a short pause he answers briefly: **„No.”** The host notes that he is not the first interlocutor who answered her that way and that this opens up a feeling of hopelessness, because Croatia is after all a smaller country than Poland.

Andrijanić nevertheless concludes with hope. He recounts his wife's conversation with a Croatian woman, who said that God in decisive moments always sends true statesmen to nations that are faithful to him. Croats had **Tuđman** when they needed him, and Poles now have Nawrocki. The guest believes that soon a man could appear in Croatia as well who will be „the emanation of the very best in the Croatian national being”. The host adds that one should pray for him, with which the guest agrees.

At the end, the host thanks the guest. The conversation was planned for forty-five minutes, but lasted more than an hour. Andrijanić apologizes if he was „rambling a bit”. He says that a lot has built up inside him, and when he gets the opportunity to speak in Croatian, it is hard to stop him. Both express hope that this was not their last conversation.
